item.content:encoded:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline is officially in the rearview mirror, and we're on to Week 10, where we'll see a couple of players in new uniforms this week — and some in their old uniforms.

Kirk Cousins rejoined the Minnesota Vikings this week via a trade with the Las Vegas Raiders. He will presumably don purple this weekend against the Green Bay Packers — the very team he last faced with Minnesota, when he suffered a season-ending Achilles tear. He'll look to give the offense a much-needed boost to complement Brian Flores' defense after the team's 6-2 start.

With the trade of Cousins, the Raiders officially named 2026 No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza as their starter moving forward. He'll face a tough schedule to kick off his career as a starting quarterback, with the Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos on deck in Weeks 10 and 11.

Follow along with Yahoo Sports for the latest NFL news, injury updates and more ahead of Week 10.

item.title: Lions, Patriots injury report: Amon-Ra St. Brown questionable
item.description: Taking a closer look at the Lions and Patriots injury designations for Week 10.
item.content:encoded:
The Detroit Lions (6-2) and New England Patriots (5-4) have declared their injury designations ahead of their Week 10 matchup in Munich, Germany. Both teams declared three players OUT before traveling overseas, but the rest of Detroit’s injured players will have a chance to play.

Note: Any changes from the most recent injury report will be bolded.

Ruled OUT

  • C Cade Mays (low ankle sprain)
  • CB D.J. Reed (hip)
  • S Kerby Joseph (knee, PUP) — Days remaining in injury evaluation clock: 4

Mays, Reed, and Joseph didn’t travel with the team to Germany and were unofficially ruled out on Thursday; that status was confirmed on Friday. The good news for the Lions is that no other injured players were designated out, meaning the rest of the roster will have a chance to play in this game.

Look for Juice Scruggs to start at center in place of Mays, with an outside-corner rotation that will likely lean on Rock Ya-Sin to start. Joseph remains on the PUP list, and a decision on his roster status will happen early next week.

Questionable

  • RB Sione Vaki (ankle) — Upgraded to a limited practice
  • WR Amon-Ra St. Brown (rib)

Vaki was a late addition to the injury report last week but played through the injury against the Dolphins. He did not practice Wednesday or Thursday, but returned to the field Friday for a walkthrough, giving him a chance to play Sunday. The fact that they brought him along on the trip is a strong indication that they believe he’ll have a chance to play against the Patriots.

St. Brown was limited in all three practices this week, but the idea that he may not play in this game is laughable. Playing in this game is quite literally “a dream come true’ for St. Brown, and there is no way he misses this opportunity.

Not listed with an injury designation

  • QB Jared Goff (chest)
  • RB Jacob Saylors (neck/hamstring)
  • EDGE DJ Wonnum (concussion)
  • S Brian Branch (hip)

The players listed in this section are not listed with a game designation and therefore are expected to play on Sunday. Coach Dan Campbell downplayed Goff’s injury at his morning press conference, noting that they’re required to list him on the report if there are any potential issues, but there isn’t anything to be concerned about.

Patriots’ injury designations

Already Ruled OUT:

  • RB2 TreVeyon Henderson (illness)
  • LG Ben Brown (knee)
  • CB Carlton Davis III (knee)

Full report to come.

A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) could return this week after a multi-week absence when the New England Patriots face the Detroit Lions in Munich. Brown traveled with the team to Germany and, along with running back Rhamondre Stevenson (knee), has looked "pretty good" in practice this week, according to head coach Mike Vrabel.

Brown has been limited to three games this season and has been out since Week 7. He is listed as questionable for Sunday, along with Stevenson.

After sitting out last week while in concussion protocol, Deshaun Watson will be back under center for the Cleveland Browns on Sunday. Shedeur Sanders got the start against the New Orleans Saints in Week 9, but head coach Todd Monken announced this week that Watson is healthy enough to start.

San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans (Achilles) won't be rushed back with the team sitting 7-1 and atop the NFC West. The veteran is unlikely to play this week against the Dallas Cowboys, but after missing the past two games Evans is progressing well.

"I think it is getting real close," Shanahan said KNBR. "But we look at it at the beginning of the week, every week, and see where he's at, and he was a lot closer this week than last week, and hopefully, that continues next week."

Willis has been playing through a groin injury and, after undergoing an MRI, it showed he is dealing with a core muscle issue. Nacua sustained his injuries in Week 9. item.title: Fantasy Football Start 'Em, Sit 'Em: Justin Boone's Week 10 lineup advice
item.description: Fantasy football analyst Justin Boone delivers his lineup advice for Week 10.
item.content:encoded:
Justin Boone provides a weekly look at undervalued fantasy players to consider starting this week and potential busts you might want to leave on your bench. 

For the rest of your lineup decisions, consult his Week 10 rankings. 

Starts

Tyler Shough, QB, Saints

vs. Panthers

Shough has been fairly predictable through the Saints’ first eight games this season. In the four games where he’s played defenses in the top half of the league for most points allowed to quarterbacks, Shough has finished as a top-eight fantasy QB each time. However, in the other four contests against stronger defenses, he’s been the QB15 or worse. 

While the Panthers are technically giving up the 13th fewest fantasy points to passers this year, those numbers are misleading when you factor in the injuries to starters like Jaycee Horn and Bobby Okereke. The Saints offense is also getting healthier after the returns of first-round rookie wideout Jordyn Tyson and left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. last week. 

The most intriguing aspect of this contest is the potential volume. Both teams rank inside the top seven in neutral pace of play this season and the game has a very solid projected point total of 49.5. That has Shough firmly inside my top-10 at the position this week. 

Other QBs to start:

  • Patrick Mahomes at Falcons – While it might take Josh Downs some time to learn the offense in Kansas City, his presence is a boost for the Chiefs’ passing attack. Mahomes has multiple touchdown passes in six of his eight outings this year. Now, he gets a Falcons defense that’s permitted three top-10 QB results, including Joe Burrow’s four-touchdown effort last Sunday.  

  • Bryce Young at Saints – Young benefitted from an easier schedule in the early part of the season, before struggling in some tougher matchups. Fortunately, he’s coming off a quality performance versus a tough Broncos defense. That bodes well for him in what projects to be an uptempo game against the Saints, who are allowing the 12th most fantasy points to QBs. 

Ollie Gordon II, RB, Dolphins

at Colts

Malik Willis heading to injured reserve is a concerning development for a young Dolphins offense that had been showing promise in recent weeks. While his absence will be a serious problem in tougher matchups, it shouldn’t derail Gordon this week against his easiest opponent yet.

The Colts are the fourth most generous defense to fantasy running backs and are heading in the wrong direction over the last couple of weeks after trading away defensive stalwart DeForest Buckner. Indy has been hit hard by Bhayshul Tuten (159 yards, two TDs), Chris Rodriguez Jr. (58 yards, TD), Javonte Williams (124 yards, TD) and Tyler Goodson (77 yards) over the past two games alone. 

Gordon continues to be productive, even in more difficult matchups, but this is a spot for a spike week as the offense leans on him with Kyle McCord under center. 

Other RBs to start:

  • Jonathan Taylor vs. Dolphins – Despite a brief decline in playing time the last couple of weeks while rumors swirled about a potential trade, Taylor remained with Indy. With the Colts being favored by four points, I’m expecting to see his touches rise against the Dolphins. Miami is also allowing the eighth most fantasy points to RBs, including double-digit fantasy points to at least one running back each week. 

  • Breece Hall vs. Bills – In his first game back from injury, Hall played fewer snaps than backup Braelon Allen, but dominated volume with 19 touches for 87 scrimmage yards against the Chiefs’ tough run defense. That’s a much tougher draw than this week’s opponent, the Bills, who are the 10th easiest defense for fantasy RBs in 2026. 

  • Zach Charbonnet at Raiders – Charbonnet assumed the lead back role in his second game since returning from a torn ACL, playing 56% of the snaps and turning 17 touches into 86 yards versus the Cardinals. Next up is a Raiders defense that’s been a springboard for fantasy RBs, allowing the third most points to the position, including seven top-12 weekly results in nine outings. 

Tetairoa McMillan, WR, Panthers

vs. Saints

If you can’t tell, I’m targeting the Saints-Panthers game pretty heavily for fantasy. 

McMillan has been solid but not spectacular this season, especially when the matchups have been more challenging. He’s failed to top 60 yards in any of the past three games against the Bucs, Packers and Broncos, but thankfully a touchdown saved his fantasy day in Week 9.  

Though the Saints aren’t exactly a pushover this week, they have let six different receivers post double-digit points in the past five outings. That includes both Browns wideouts hitting the mark last Sunday with KC Concepcion amassing 85 yards and a touchdown, while Denzel Boston poured in 98 yards. 

This is a spot to confidently play both McMillan and Jalen Coker as fantasy WR2s. 

Other WRs to start:

  • Zay Flowers vs. Chargers – The arrival of Jacoby Brissett breathes life back into Flowers’ fantasy outlook. While it might take some time for their connection to form, Flowers should be productive this week against a Chargers defense that’s the fifth-softest matchup for receivers and allowed five touchdowns to the Texans’ wideouts in Week 9. 

  • Rashee Rice at Falcons – For all the flak sent in Rice’s direction this season, he’s managed to produce against a difficult schedule. All five of his appearances have come against defenses in the top-12 for fewest fantasy points allowed to his position, but he’s still averaging WR24 stats on a per game basis. The Falcons are actually the most generous defense he’s faced on paper, giving up the 13th most points to WRs. 

  • DJ Moore at Jets – In his three healthy games before last week, Moore had posted 100 yards and a TD versus the Texans, 67 yards against the Chargers, as well as 82 yards and a TD against the Ravens. Don’t let a down game in a matchup with a fierce Vikings defense scare you away. Moore is a fantasy WR2 with WR1 upside most weeks. 

Tyler Warren, TE, Colts

vs. Dolphins

With Josh Downs and Keenan Allen traded away, Tyler Warren is the only proven pass-catcher remaining in the Colts offense. He’s currently averaging the fourth most targets among tight ends, but he’ll challenge for the league lead in that category the rest of the way. 

The only question is whether he can capitalize on the volume in a struggling Colts offense. While the added defensive attention will be a problem in tougher matchups, I’m not as concerned about it this week. 

The Dolphins are the fourth easiest opponent for fantasy tight ends and the Colts are somehow favored in this game. That means you can start Warren as a top-five option at the position. 

Other TEs to start:

  • Darren Waller at Saints – Waller is a boom-or-bust fantasy TE2, who’s coming off his biggest boom of the year with eight catches, 90 yards and a touchdown on 10 targets against the Broncos. The Saints are another favorable opponent, allowing the seventh most fantasy points to TEs. 

  • Tyler Higbee at Cardinals – Higbee had a three-game streak with over 60 yards in each outing, before failing to reach 25 yards in any of his past four appearances. However, with Puka Nacua, Davante Adams and Terrance Ferguson sidelined, Higbee is back in the mix as a volume-based TE2 streamer. 

Sits

Kirk Cousins, QB, Vikings

at Packers

Jonathan Gannon has the Packers defense playing extremely well and that’s been without Micah Parsons, who is nearing a return in the coming weeks. Green Bay has held six of the last eight quarterbacks it’s encountered to one touchdown or less. 

The excitement around Cousins' return to Minnesota is well deserved and will result in some fantastic fantasy performances between now and the end of the season. But I’m taking a cautious approach in his first start since the trade. 

Cousins projects as a risky QB2 versus the Packers and there are simply better streaming options available at the position. 

Other QBs to sit:

  • Matthew Stafford at Cardinals – Stafford hasn’t thrown for more than 228 yards in any game over the last month and has been held to just a single touchdown in each of his past two contests. Now, he’ll try to get by without Puka Nacua. Even in a good matchup, it’s hard to trust Stafford given his current weapons. 

  • Fernando Mendoza vs. Seahawks – While I’m optimistic that Klint Kubiak can get the most out of Mendoza over the final two months, this isn’t the game for fantasy managers to start the rookie. Seattle is the second worst matchup for fantasy QBs. 

Quinshon Judkins, RB, Browns

vs. Texans

Judkins has only played 39% and 34% of the snaps during his last two games, which coincides with the return of backup Dylan Sampson. 

We might want to put backup in quotes since Sampson has out-snapped (96-52) and out-gained (117-94) Judkins during that span, with Judkins being held under 50 scrimmage yards in both contests and not finding the end zone. 

To make matters worse, Sampson has the bigger role as a pass-catcher, limiting Judkins’ fantasy outlook even more. The Texans aren’t a bad matchup, but if Judkins didn’t come through in an ideal setup against the Saints last week, I don’t have much faith in him delivering here. 

Consider this backfield a 50-50 split with Judkins being more of a TD-or-bust fantasy RB3 moving forward. 

Other RBs to sit:

  • Tyler Allgeier vs. Rams – With Bam Knight expected to return this week, Allgeier won’t dominate work the way he did in Week 9. Arizona will also be dealing with a Rams defense that’s allowing the fourth-fewest fantasy points to RBs. 

  • Kaleb Johnson vs. Vikings – Johnson will likely lead the Packers’ backfield with Josh Jacobs sidelined, but unfortunately the next three weeks involve bad matchups with the Vikings and Rams, sandwiched around a bye. He’s a TD-or-bust flex option due to a limited receiving role. 

  • Omarion Hampton at Ravens – Hampton is still in a three-way committee and hasn’t topped 60 scrimmage yards in six games. He’s another TD-or-bust flex option. 

DK Metcalf, WR, Steelers

at Bengals

Metcalf is preparing for another battle with DJ Turner and the Bengals defense. We know Metcalf is the kind of streaky receiver who can erupt in any contest, but he’s been held to 50 yards or less in each of his last three meetings with Cincinnati. 

That includes a three-catch, 31-yard outing against them in Week 3, which he salvaged with a touchdown. 

The outlook is similar here, with Metcalf being a risky fantasy WR3 who will likely need a TD to come through for his managers. 

Other WRs to sit:

  • Tre Tucker vs. Seahawks – Tucker had three spike-weeks this season, but has been held under 60 yards in every other game. This isn’t the week to chase a big performance against the Seahawks defense that’s allowing the fewest fantasy points to WRs. 

  • Keenan Allen at Cowboys – After being traded to San Francisco, Allen is suiting up against the Cowboys for the second straight week. As a member of the Colts, he only managed 26 yards on four catches last Sunday. While he’s the type of veteran receiver who could get up to speed quickly with his new club, it’s very risky to trust him in his first game with a Niners team that has only had one WR top 40 yards in each of their last five contests. 

  • Khalil Shakir at Jets – Shakir is a low-ceiling volume play who hasn’t topped 25 yards in any of his last three games versus the Jets. He’s an option if you’re in a bye-week pinch, but don’t get your hopes up for a big game this week. 

Brenton Strange, TE, Jaguars

at Titans

Strange has only seen two targets each of the last two weeks, as the Jags have been able to lean on their rushing attack en route to easy victories. 

It seems logical we’ll see more of the same with Jacksonville entering this game as 10.5-point favorites over the Titans. 

That makes Strange a low-volume fantasy TE2, who will likely need to score a touchdown before things get out of hand. 

Other TEs to sit:

  • Mike Gesicki vs. Steelers – Six touchdowns in eight games has been impressive, but Gesicki is threading a very thin needle with 11 yards or less in three of his last four outings. He’s just a TD-or-bust TE2 against Pittsburgh. 

  • Mark Andrews vs. Chargers – While the arrival of Jacoby Brissett is good news for the Ravens’ passing attack, it doesn’t change the outlook for Andrews. The veteran hasn’t eclipsed 30 yards in five straight games. His playing time is also on the decline, at under 60% of the snaps the last three weeks.

item.title: Carnell Tate injury update: Titans rookie WR to miss second straight game
item.description: A lengthy injury report for the Titans coming off the bye.
item.content:encoded:
Robert Saleh said today that Tennessee Titans rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate will miss his second straight game with a shoulder injury. There was some hope that he would be ready with the Titans being off last week, but it will be at least one more week. You already knew a Titans rookie receiver couldn’t make it through a whole season without being injured.

Unfortunately, the injury report doesn’t stop there. Saleh also ruled out guard Peter Skoronski (hamstring), linebackers Anthony Hill (neck) and Cody Barton (concussion), and punter Tommy Townsend (knee). The Titans haven’t placed any of those players on injured reserve yet, so the hope is that they will all be back sooner rather than later.

The injuries at linebacker will allow Cedric Gray to play the entire game. Gray was one of the best players on defense for the Titans this year, but the new staff hasn’t been eager to get him on the field.

The only good news today is that the Jaguars announced that safety Jessie Bates and defensive tackle Jordan Davis will not play against the Titans. Neither of those players has had their bye week yet, and with the Jaguars already having theirs, the team decided to give them this week off. I could make a comment here about teams viewing the Titans as a bye week, but I won’t.

A game at home might be […]
item.content:encoded:
Kirk Cousins leads the Minnesota Vikings into Green Bay to take on the last place Green Bay Packers. The Packers come into the game in good form, particularly quarterback Jordan Love. Love played better against the Vikings defense than anyone else has this year in the Week 1 matchup. A game at home might be exactly what they need to maintain that momentum. That means the Vikings will likely need their returning quarterback, Kirk Cousins, to play well immediately. They will likely need to score more than the average 18 points.

Series Record: 62-67-3

Road Record: 28-36-3

Streak: W2

Largest Victory: 42-7, September 28, 1986

Largest Defeat: 45-7, November 14, 2011

  • 27 of the last 48 regular season games in this series have been decided by 7 or fewer points.
  • The NFC North’s 25-9 record is the best any division has had through nine weeks since the 2002 divisional realignment.
  • The Packers come in with the 2nd most pass yards per game in the NFL on offense (279.7); the Minnesota Vikings come in with the 2nd fewest passing yards allowed per game (161.1).
  • The Packers are terrible at running the ball, averaging a league worst 68.2 yards per game. That’s typically the weak spot for the Viking defense.
  • Kirk Cousins is 6-4-1 in his career against the Packers with a 106.7 Passer Rating.
  • Cousins has 14 TDs and 0 INTs in the wins and 5 TDs with 7 INTs in the losses.

It’s fitting for Kirk’s first game back to be on the field that ended his time in Minnesota. It’s going to be a tough ask for him to come in and lead this team against a better than average Packers’ defense. Jordan Love had the most success of any quarterback against the Vikings’ defense in Week 1. He’s in better form now than he was then. However, I believe the Vikings will come out fired up. They will be inspired by the return of their captain Kirk Cousins. The team has indicated they’re ready for a Super Bowl run with this defense and it will start on Sunday. The Packers are going down at home and they’ll stay in the basement where they belong.

Vikings 23 – Packers 20

item.content:encoded:
Officially, Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown is questionable for Sunday's game against the Patriots in Germany with a rib injury. Unofficially, it is extraordinarily unlikely that St. Brown would miss this game.

St. Brown has always been more than willing to play through injuries, and this game means a lot to him because his mother is German, he speaks fluent German, and he has been circling this game on his calendar as an important one for him personally.

Three Lions have been ruled out: safety Kerby Joseph, center Cade Mays and cornerback DJ Reed. Joining St. Brown as questionable is running back Sione Vaki.

Other Lions dealing with injuries this week are quarterback Jared Goff, safety Brian Branch, running back Jacob Saylors and pass rusher DJ Wonnum, but they all practiced in full the last two days and will be good to go on Sunday.

item.title: Fantasy Football Usage Report: Tank Dell flashes in second game back from injury
item.description: Zachary Krueger takes a look at exciting and worrisome performances from Week 9 of the 2026 NFL season.
item.content:encoded:
With roughly five weeks left in the fantasy football regular season, we continue to navigate bye weeks (CHI, DEN, PHI, and TB in Week 10) and devastating injuries, like that to Arizona Cardinals wide receiver Michael Wilson (neck).

Regardless, the fantasy season presses on, and we'll navigate whatever comes our way as we look to secure our spots in the fantasy postseason and chase ultimate glory at season's end. With several key players out this week — for one reason or another, here are a few players whose recent usage has caught my eye as we enter Week 10.

RotoPat’s Week 10 Fantasy Football Rankings
Ranking and evaluating all of Week 10’s top plays at quarterback, running back, receiver, tight end, kicker and defense.
  • Patrick Daugherty,

▶ Running Backs

Dylan Sampson (CLE) vs. Saints

Since returning from the knee injury that sidelined him Weeks 2 through 6, Dylan Sampson has appeared on 55 percent of the Browns' snaps compared to Quinshon Judkins, who has been in on 42 percent of the snaps. Sampson's 32 opportunities over that span narrowly trail Judkins' (47), but over the last two weeks, those numbers look much closer, and Sampson looks like a PPR scam waiting to happen.

Sampson's 14 targets over the last two weeks are good for most of any running back in the league over that span, while his nine receptions are tied for second-most, and his 89 yards are good for third-most. The 30 routes he ran in last week's loss to the Saints were the most he has run in his career, but it is worth noting that he needed the game to go to overtime for that to happen.

Regardless, Sampson appears to have a solid grasp of the pass-catching role in the Browns' backfield, and his production has averaged 10.5 PPR points per game since Week 7. He'll be on the streaming radar this week against a Texans defense that ranks 20th in points allowed to opposing RBs this season.

Jadarian Price (SEA) vs. Cardinals

After sharing the backfield for two weeks with Zach Charbonnet, rookie first-rounder Jadarian Price has had little to offer his fantasy managers. Price has averaged 13.5 opportunities per game and 57.5 yards from scrimmage per game since Week 8, but his efficiency on the ground, 19-53-0 (2.8 YPC), leaves much to be desired, especially in the high-value areas of the field.

Neither Price nor Charbonnet has had a chance to carry the ball inside their opponents' five-yard line over the last two weeks, but it's worth pointing out that last season, Charbonnet's 18 carries in that area of the field were more than double what Kenneth Walker (8) saw last season. In the three games he played before his injury, Price received only one carry in that area of the field, so it's fair to assume any touchdowns that may come his way will need to come on explosive plays.

The double-digit opportunities are encouraging, but Price's slow start, coupled with Charbonnet firmly back in the mix, makes him hard to trust entering Week 10 against the Raiders.

Week 10 Best and Worst WR, TE Matchups: Jalen Coker, Darren Waller in great spot vs. Saints
Denny Carter breaks down which secondaries are struggling against slot and boundary pass catchers to help you set your Week 10 lineups.
  • Denny Carter,

▶ Wide Receivers

Tank Dell (HOU) vs. Chargers

In just his second game back from a devastating knee injury he suffered late in the 2024 season, Tank Dell looked like the explosive receiver we saw during the first two seasons of his career in Week 9's win over the Chargers. Dell's 105 receiving yards in Sunday's win were second only to Kayshon Boutte (125), but his nine targets led all Texans receivers, while his 22 routes ranked third-most, but well behind Xavier Hutchinson (34) and Nico Collins (31).

Dell's 40.9 percent targets-per-route rate also set a very impressive mark, but we shouldn't be surprised to see C.J. Stroud target him as heavily as he did. For his career, Dell has been targeted on a respectable 20.6 percent of his routes, and he has seen seven or more targets in 14 of his 27 career games. Dell ran only six routes in Week 8, which was his first game in nearly two years. While Week 9's game was encouraging for multiple reasons, it's possible Dell continues to see an uptick in snaps and routes in the weeks ahead if he continues to play well and shows that his knee is holding up after a few games.

Another encouraging sign for Dell is that on his 63-yard touchdown reception, he hit speeds up to 20.09 MPH, which ranked 14th fastest among all ball carriers in the league in Week 9, per NFL Next Gen Stats. Dell has some deep league FLEX appeal this week against the Browns as he looks to build on his breakout performance and show he is fully back and healthy.

Marvin Harrison Jr. (HOU) vs. Chargers

It feels like everything that could have gone wrong for Marvin Harrison Jr. since his trade to the Texans has gone wrong. In his first week with the team, Jaylin Noel popped up for 107 yards and one touchdown against the Jags. In Week 8, Harrison was fortunate enough to find the end zone despite running only eight routes, and then in Week 9 he watched two of his teammates top 100 receiving yards while he was held to 2-20-0 on three targets while running only 14 routes.

We knew it would take a few weeks for Harrison to get up to speed after being traded mid-season from the Cardinals, but with so many receivers playing well ahead of him, it's genuinely hard to imagine him carving out a meaningful role for Houston as long as most of its receivers are healthy. Fantasy managers who are still holding Harrison in hopes that his reuniting with Stroud would lead to some kind of second-half bounce back will need to keep waiting, as Harrison's path to fantasy relevance continues to look muddied.

▶ Tight Ends

Darren Waller (CAR) vs. Broncos

We shouldn't expect Darren Waller to see another 10-target performance like he had last week against the Broncos, when he caught eight passes for 90 yards and a touchdown in what ended up being the most productive game in his career since 2023. Waller's 23.0 PPR-point performance was good for the TE2 overall in Week 9, and while he may not replicate it this week, he does draw a plus matchup against a Saints defense that has allowed the seventh-most points to opposing tight ends this season.

Waller, in his first season with the Panthers, has been surprisingly involved in the offense this season. Now appearing to be fully healthy, the 34-year-old tight end leads all Panthers tight ends in routes (197), and has posted four double-digit PPR performances in the eight games he has appeared in this season. While his target volume has been unreliable at times, seeing three or fewer targets on five separate occasions, Waller has also seen decent involvement near the end zone, with three of his four touchdowns coming when targeted in the end zone.

Fantasy managers in need of a streaming option this week can treat Waller as a boom-or-bust TE2, who could find the end zone against a Saints defense that has given up a touchdown to opposing tight ends in each of its last three games.

Mike Gesicki (CIN) vs. Falcons

For most of the season, Mike Gesicki has managed "get away with it" for those who may have opted to trust him after his 18.8 PPR point outburst in Week 1. The current TE15 in fantasy points per game this season has turned in a top-12 PPR performance in four of the eight games he has played in, but ranks outside the top 20 at his position in receiving yards (00), receptions (00), and targets (00), with pure touchdown volume carrying his day.

Gesicki has found the end zone in six games this season. Twice, his touchdown was his only reception of the game. His 191 routes run are tied for 23 among tight ends this season, and he draws a matchup against a Steelers defense that has allowed the 12th-fewest fantasy points to opposing tight ends this season. Last week's 3.1 PPR point performance is the kind of performance we should be expecting from Gesicki whenever he isn't finding the end zone, and in his two one-touchdown/one-catch games, he finished as the TE22 in both of those weeks.

item.description: Scott Pianowski plays traffic cop, sharing some start/sit advice for key players in fantasy football for Week 10.
item.content:encoded:
Start-sit decisions can be vexing for even the best of fantasy football managers. If you need help setting your fantasy football lineups, Scott Pianowski offers some assistance with his Week 10 traffic report.

Green Light ✅

RB Corey Kiner vs. Lions (Germany): The Detroit run defense has decent numbers, but they're artificially inflated by a favorable schedule. Kiner has been New England's most efficient back all year, and he's likely to start and get 15-20 touches in this spot with TreVeyon Henderson out and Rhamondre Stevenson’s status in doubt. Sounds like RB2 music.

RB Zach Charbonnet at Raiders: He was the main runner last week, while Jadarian Price was the primary pass-catcher. The rushing role is the simpler path to fantasy relevance, and with the Seahawks favored by 6.5 points, game script should work in his favor. The Raiders have been horrible against the run all season, too.

RB Ollie Gordon II at Colts: The Dolphins are starting an untested QB this week (Kyle McCord), so don't be surprised when Gordon has a monster workload Sunday. The Indianapolis defense hasn't stopped much this year, but it's especially weak against the run (31st in DVOA).

WR Jordan Watkins at Cowboys: The San Francisco WR room is badly in need of some youth, and that's where the sophomore Watkins can help. He's produced a useful 7-142-1 line over the last two games, and it's possible Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel Sr. will both be out Sunday. On the other side is the Dallas defense, which hasn't stopped much of anything in 2026.

Yellow Light 😕

WR Justin Jefferson at Packers: It might take time for the Kirk Cousins' return to really click, though it's nice that he already has extensive history with his teammates. Jefferson's biggest problem in Week 10 might be the Green Bay defense, which is surprisingly the fourth-best pass defense in the league, per DVOA. The Cousins trade likely saved Jefferson's season, but let's wait a few weeks for things to settle in.

WR Wan'Dale Robinson vs. Jaguars: With Carnell Tate out again, the Robinson PPR scam might be open for business. Robinson quietly has 21 catches in his last four games, and although you never think of him as an end-zone factor, he's also spiked three times in his last six starts. With a messy WR landscape staring at us, Robinson is in the WR3 conversation here.

QB Aaron Rodgers at Bengals: His fantasy production is moving in the wrong direction, dropping for three straight starts. But the schedule sets up favorably, as the Steelers are rested off the bye and the Bengals return from a Europe trip. Rodgers also solved this defense in the first meeting, throwing for 292 yards and three touchdown. He's at the top of the streamer list for Week 10.

TE Darren Waller at Saints: His production has not been consistent this year, but he's capable of cooking in a plus matchup (he wrecked the seam-leaky Broncos last week, returning 8-90-2). The Saints are the seventh-easiest matchup for opposing tight ends, so we'll keep the light on for Waller in the dome.

Red Light 🚨

RB Quinshon Judkins vs. Texans: The Texans are still a plus defense against the run, and Judkins hasn't been elusive for most of his second year (3.3 YPC). And if the game script goes away for Cleveland, that's going to benefit pass-catching RB Dylan Sampson, not Judkins.

WR Caleb Douglas at Colts: He's made it to 70 yards in two of the last three weeks, notable production given the limitations of Malik Willis. But Douglas can't be viewed as a proactive start until we see what the Dolphins have with new quarterback Kyle McCord.

RB Chase Brown vs. Steelers: He's stuck on one touchdown for the year and Samaje Perine is cutting into the workload of late. Pittsburgh is also a nasty Week 10 draw, the sixth-hardest defense for backs to score against. The Cincinnati passing game is a sight to behold, but Brown has always been a good, not great, talent.

TE Tucker Kraft vs. Vikings: He's been the odd man out in Green Bay's glorious passing season, perhaps to be expected given that Kraft is just a calendar year removed from an ACL tear. The Vikings are the wrong team for Kraft to bounce back against, the NFL's stingiest defense against opposing tight ends. Kraft needs a show-me game before he's back in the Circle of Trust.

item.title: Week 10 Fantasy Football Bold Predictions: Ravens offense gets back on track with Jacoby Brissett
item.description: Our fantasy football staff goes over their bold predictions for Week 10.
item.content:encoded:
We’re into the second half of the 2026 fantasy football season, and while we have a big sample size of data to work off, the NFL landscape is ever-changing. We have plenty of new QBs starting in Week 10, whether due to a trade or injury. That makes things tougher to predict. But our Yahoo analysts are giving it a go, sharing their bold predictions for the slate.

Derrick Henry returns to King status

Jacoby Brissett is off to Baltimore and Derrick Henry’s fantasy value can be saved! He’s set up for a perfect bounce back spot against the Los Angeles Chargers on Monday Night Football. For Baltimore, this is a must-win game to stay with the leaders of the AFC, and the Ravens have shown they’ll run Henry to the ground when necessary. Last week without their top two quarterbacks, Henry carried the ball on 61% of his snaps on a day when the Ravens’ starting quarterback posted negative fantasy points.

As long as the backup QB hasn’t been horrible, neither has Henry, far from it actually, averaging nearly 20 PPG in the five games with Tyler Huntley since arriving to Baltimore. I believe in Brissett’s ability to lead this run-heavy attack against a Chargers defense whose matchup rank is a little bit of a lie, ranking first versus receiving backs (a near non-factor for Henry) but 28th versus rushing fantasy points. Henry will finish with 100+ rushing yards and a TD for the first time since Week 1. — Joel Smyth

Zay Flowers joins in on the fun against Chargers on MNF

The matchup supports a good night for Baltimore’s top receiving option, and my projections already have Flowers seeing more than eight targets with 84 receiving yards. The Chargers use 78% zone coverage and 38% press coverage, giving Baltimore reasons to work underneath. The Ravens send 39% of their targets on in-breaking routes, seventh-highest in the league. That combination points toward opportunities across the middle, where Flowers can catch the ball in stride and create additional yardage.

The Chargers have also allowed a receiver to exceed 70 yards in three consecutive games. Flowers’ projected target volume puts him in position to extend that streak and take it further. Those underneath completions offer new quarterback Jacoby Brissett a way to establish a rhythm while keeping Flowers involved throughout the game. The opportunity is there for repeated touches, yards after the catch and a touchdown to turn that workload into a big fantasy performance. Flowers goes for 100+ receiving yards and a score. — Ray Garvin

Jalen Coker reaches top-18 WR status for second time this season

The last time Jalen Coker hit top-18 status was Week 1. The Panthers are a pretty straightforward team, if the offensive line doesn’t get overwhelmed, they stay aggressive and attack every blade of grass. Even though the Saints have created 13 sacks over their past three games, much of that comes from blitzing (60th percentile), as they rank in the 10th percentile in pressure rate without the blitz. But most notably, the Saints utilize single high coverage 65% of the time, the second-highest mark in the league. We have seen Coker be an absolute menace in these single-high looks with vertical routes. Just like against the Bears in the season opener. — Josh Norris

Aaron Rodgers gets it going with top-10 QB finish

The Steelers offense really found its groove before the bye week. The team leaned into its strong ground game and heavy personnel groupings. The game that really started their identity shift was back in Week 3 against this Bengals defense. While Cincy is objectively better defensively, they have clear lines of attack for teams to pick on; run away from Dexter Lawrence to the outside and target the linebackers and safeties in coverage. Pittsburgh’s offense is well-equipped to do just that.

With Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle successfully moving the ball on the ground, this team should be in scoring areas often. Rodgers and this offense have a high passing rate in the red zone and their personnel match up well against the areas the Bengals are weakest on defense. Germie Bernard is a strong over the middle target and both tight ends are mismatches. I see Rodgers at least throwing two touchdowns with plenty of yardage to match. — Matt Harmon

Dylan Sampson leads Cleveland in receptions

The Cleveland running game has been stuck in neutral all year, which is a comment on both Quinshon Judkins and the offensive line. The Houston defense, while an overall disappointment, still stops the run well. And if the Browns fall behind as expected, Deshaun Watson can start the PPR scam working with Sampson, something we saw six times in the last Watson start. Dear readers can decide if Sampson getting lots of dump-off work is more of a feature or bug; often those types of passes are available because the opponent is conceding them. But if you're desperate for a RB3/flex play in a tricky week, Sampson has a case worth considering. — Scott Pianowski

Chris Olave gives us back-to-back WR1 finishes

Chris Olave isn’t a normal WR1. For example, we’d like our top receiver to get easy passes tossed their way. Olave gives those the nah wave. Of the 26 WRs with a 20+% target rate, he has the fifth-highest aDOT. And yet, he’s sixth in first downs per route run. Tyler Shough has looked for No. 12 on at least 25% of his throws in every game. In other words, opportunity, even with Jordyn Tyson coming on, shouldn’t be a problem.

Besides, the Saints and Panthers are two of five teams with top-10 marks in plays per game and pace. Plus, Carolina has struggled against receivers of Olave’s archetype. WR1s have had a floor of 13.4 PPR PPG, and receivers with a double-digit aDOT are up to 16.5 a week. The Panthers are coming into Sunday with the second-lowest pressure rate since their bye. Assuming Shough has time to let routes develop, Olave will give us his third top-10 finish in Week 10. — Chris Allen

Zach Charbonnet finishes as a top-10 fantasy RB

You can count me among those who doubted Charbonnet’s ability to make a significant fantasy impact this season after returning from a torn ACL suffered in January. However, in his second game back Charbonnet led the Seahawks’ RBs by playing 56% of the snaps, which resulted in 17 touches, 86 scrimmage yards and a win over the Cardinals. Seeing the way his performance fired up teammates and coaches, it’s clear who the preferred option is in Seattle’s backfield.

Now, the trusted veteran gets his easiest matchup yet versus a Raiders defense allowing the third-most fantasy points to running backs, including six top-10 weekly results in nine outings — Christian McCaffrey (RB4), Braelon Allen (RB7), James Cook III (RB3), Rhamondre Stevenson (RB10), Kenneth Walker III (RB2) and Omarion Hampton (RB6). That doesn’t even account for the Rams’ duo, who both finished in the top 15 against them — Kyren Williams (RB12) and Blake Corum (RB15). With the Seahawks entering the week as 6.5-point favorites, there will be plenty of positive game script for Charbonnet en route to a fantasy RB1 finish. — Justin Boone

item.title: NFL predictions: Titans-Jaguars matchup could get ugly
item.description: Can the Titans score enough points to keep this game close?
item.content:encoded:
If you didn’t already know before the last couple of weeks that the Tennessee Titans and Jacksonville Jaguars are in very different places, the two teams’ activities around the 2026 NFL trade deadline confirmed it. The Titans traded their two best defensive players for future draft picks. The Jaguars traded future draft picks for three players to solidify their defense.

The Titans are 10.5-point home underdogs in this game. As I have said many times this year, that number doesn’t feel high enough. This feels like a name-your-number type of game for Trevor Lawrence and the Jacksonville offense. They are 4th in the league in points per game at 28.6. The Titans defense ranks 22nd, allowing 24.9 points per game.

For the Titans offense, the most important thing here is to see Cam Ward build on his performance against the Cincinnati Bengals two weeks ago. You should not expect him to throw for 300 yards again; he has only done that once in his career, but he should be able to be in command of the offense. Brian Daboll pushed the right buttons in that Bengals game. This Jaguars defense is a tougher test, but they are middle of the road against the pass.

As much as it pains me to say it, I expect the Jaguars to win this game by at least two touchdowns. Their offense has been really clicking this season, with Lawrence playing the best football of his career. My hope is that the Titans will be able to do enough to make this game hit the over.

item.title: Raiders-Seahawks Week 10: 5 things to watch
item.description: How Raiders can upset Super Bowl champions
item.content:encoded:
The 4-5 Las Vegas Raiders host the 5-4 Seattle Seahawks on Sunday. Kickoff is set for 1:05 p.m. PT. Here are five keys to victory:

Be perfect on offense:

The Raiders committed five turnovers in the second half of a 38-17 road loss at the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday. The turnovers included two in the 49ers’ end zone and a Pick Six. That’s not going to work against Seattle. The Raiders are going to have to play clean in Fernando Mendoza’s start debut against that defense to have a chance.

Get to the quarterback:

Drew Lock is a game manager. The backup, who is playing for an injured Sam Darnold, is not going to wow anyone and he can be forced into making errors. The Raiders must harass him.

Use intel:

Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak was Seattle’s offensive coordinator last year when they won the Super Bowl. He knows this roster well. He needs to scheme up a win.

Brock, Brock, Brock:

The Raiders need to be carried by their best player in this game. The tight end is putting up huge numbers every week. Las Vegas has to be willed to victory by Bowers. Fernando find Brock and do it often.

Stop the run:

Las Vegas has been getting gutted by the run every week. San Francisco had 190 yards on the ground this week. Expect Seattle to try to do the same. Las Vegas has to finally stop the bleeding on the ground.

item.title: 49ers create over $5 million in cap space after tinkering with DeForest Buckner’s contract
item.description: Will the 49ers work out an extension with DeForest Buckner?
item.content:encoded:
The San Francisco 49ers converted $6.5 million of defensive tackle DeForest Buckner’s traded salary into a signing bonus, per Spotrac. The move adds two void years, creating $5.2 million in cap space this season.

Buckner is set to become a free agent after this season, so the void years are for salary cap purposes. Here’s a look at the dead cap hit numbers for Buckner through the next few seasons, per Spotrac:

2027 – $5.2m
2028: $3.9m
2029: $2.6m
2030: $1.3m

It’ll be interesting to see what kind of extension, if any, both sides work out after this season. That could all depend on how the season goes. Buckner has $161.3 million in career earnings, which is the fourth-highest among all defensive linemen currently in the NFL. It’d be a storybook ending if Buckner finishes his career where he started.

The 49ers are currently $4.9 million in the hole in 2027, but that also includes a $40.4 million cap hit from Brandon Aiyuk. There will be enough cap space to bring back Buckner.
