item.title: Pick Six: Buffalo Bills at New York Jets
item.description: Things to watch for when the Jets take on the Bills on Sunday
item.content:encoded:
The Jets will be a home underdog against the Buffalo Bills on Sunday, having lost seven of their last eight games. Other than a last-gasp loss to the Patriots in week four, the Bills’ record is unblemished this year. Surely the Jets can’t pull off an upset, can they?

Here are six storylines to watch as New York seeks to flip their season on its head:

It’s a trap!

America is already looking ahead to the Bills-Chiefs game scheduled to take place in the evening of Thanksgiving Thursday. While Buffalo has two games to play between now and then, they will feel good about their chances of still only having one loss after playing the Jets this week and Miami next week. Kansas City has lost just twice so this could be decisive in the race for the AFC’s top seed.

We’ve seen situations like this before though. While the Jets are rarely the team to take advantage of the opportunity, their profile as a team that has kept a lot of games close and come up just short in the end could make them dangerous if the Bills get complacent.

And if they did get complacent, who could blame them? After all, the last time these teams met, the Bills rested all of their starters and still won 35-8. Then again, that was a very different Jets team too. The only current non-offensive line starters who started that game are Harrison Phillips, Jamien Sherwood and Adonai Mitchell.

Can Mitchell bounce back?

It’s become traditional this year to have at least one high profile player that doesn’t get the ball on offense. Last week, it was Adonai Mitchell, a player who seven days earlier, had posted the best numbers of his career.

The Jets really seem to be struggling with the whole “many mouths to feed” aspect of having provided their quarterback with an adequate number of pass catching weapons for the first time in several seasons. However, Mitchell not seeing the ball last week was not for the want of trying as he was thrown to seven times.

Opening drive success

We could easily spend column inches here talking about why the Jets can’t convert in the red zone, or how they shouldn’t abandon the running game, or when are they ever going to intercept another pass, but how about we discuss something they have actually been doing well?

For each of the past five games, the Jets have driven downfield and scored on their opening possession, which has played a big part in them still being competitive heading into the second half of each game. So, now we have to ask the question – can this continue? And…how will the team react if it doesn’t?

This isn’t the first time in recent memory that the offensive has looked good early on in games, and executed the scripted part of the gameplan effectively, only to then go on to struggle in the second half when points are needed to convert wins. Back in 2020, where Adam Gase’s Jets were in danger of going winless until very late in the season, they actually scored eight times in a row on their opening drive. The current decision makers would ideally not like to have too many similarities to that 2020 team.

Gregory Rousseau’s ascent to super-stardom

The biggest threat on the Bills defense is obviously edge rusher Gregory Rousseau, who is having a monster year. After just eight games, Rousseau has already tied his career-high with eight sacks, while also doubling his career mark for passes defensed with another eight.

Rousseau primarily lines up on the left, so it will be mostly up to Armand Membou to try and keep him quiet. Rousseau had a two sack game against the Jets in his second season in 2022, but surprisingly otherwise only has one sack in eight other games against the Jets. The Bills are 7-2 in these matchups, though.

Having not been traded, is Will McDonald’s role going to change?

The Jets opted not to trade former first round pick Will McDonald during the week, despite reports of interest from a number of teams. Head coach Aaron Glenn has been suggesting McDonald is still very much in the Jets plans for the rest of this season, and he is of course under contract for next year after New York exercised his fifth year option. He even implied McDonald had earned a bigger role.

McDonald’s defensive snap count percentage has dropped from 66% in both 2024 and 2025 to just 46% in 2026 and, even more confoundingly, his percentage of run snaps has increased.

Will an increase in playing time for McDonald happen on Sunday? And, if it does, are we destined to see diminishing returns in regard to his production?

What’s the plan for the secondary?

A matchup against the team with the number one offense in the entire NFL is not really the ideal time to experiment with line-up changes but the Jets are desperately striving for more consistency from their back seven, in addition to having an undermanned front that is struggling to stop the run.

Having missed a meeting and made some on-field mistakes, the previous starting slot corner – Jarvis Brownlee Jr. – is in the doghouse. However, rookie D’Angelo Ponds has looked overmatched at times which is hardly surprising given how he is learning a new position and missed half of training camp.

New York also experimented with using Minkah Fitzpatrick in the slot on Sunday, elevating Malachi Moore into the lineup at safety for basically the first time all year. Could this be the answer? Time will tell.

Let us know how you see things going in Sunday’s game in the comments section…

item.title: NFLSU rookie check-in: Week 10
item.description: A down week for the class, but a couple of great performances were sprinkled throughout.
item.content:encoded:
CB Mansoor Delane

Sadly, Delane missed the Chiefs’ last game, but he should be back for Week 10!

Kansas City will be playing the Atlanta Falcons, a team that was selling at the deadline and is having a bad season. Delane will have a tough matchup against WR Drake London, and it’ll be interesting to see how he handles the physical receiver. Also, Delane will be tasked with tackling RB Bijan Robinson, which is nearly impossible.

Safety A.J. Haulcy

Haulcy was also out for his game this past week, which was unfortunate because the Colts nearly won.

In Week 10, Haulcy has a chance to make a major impact against the Miami Dolphins. QB Malik Willis is out for the rest of the season, so backup Kyle McCord, a second-year player, will be playing and making his first career start. If Haulcy can stay consistent, he could be in position to get a turnover in this game.

WR Zavion Thomas

This season has sadly gone downhill for Thomas. He started on the bench and primarily played special teams, then finally got play on the offense and did well, but now he has been prone to penalties, and his role on offense is gone. In Week 10, Thomas had an extremely costly unnecessary roughness call that caused HC Ben Johnson to remove him from the offense. What makes things worse is that Thomas actually had a kick return for a touchdown, but was called back for a holding.

The Bears will be on their bye week.

TE Bauer Sharp

For some reason, eventhough Sharp had a really great blocking performance in Week 8, he barely played in Week 9. Really not sure why, so I’m chalking it up to bad coaching.

Bucs are also on their bye week.

WR Barion Brown

Brown had by far the best performance so far. He made an incredible 52-yard catch that set the Saints up in scoring range and was able to put New Orleans in an incredible field position on the return game. If it wasn’t for a really, really bad fumble that he had on one of his punt returns, Brown could have been one of the MVPs of the Saints game.

With the New Orleans forgiving players quickly for mistakes, Brown is going to be involved primarily on special teams again, but wouldn’t be surprised if they try to get another big play from him on offense.

LB Harold Perkins

The Falcons had a tough defensive performance against the Bengals last week, but Perkins was one of the best players on their defense and had a great game (as usual). With Perkins’ health and consistent performances, I would say he has been the top player from LSU’s 2026 class.

As mentioned earlier, the Falcons will play the Chiefs, and Perkins will have to deal with RB Kenneth Walker, which is arguably his biggest challenge of the season.

QB Garrett Nussmeier

Did not play because Patrick Mahomes is healthy.

EDGE Jack Pyburn

Was waived by the Chiefs, but brought back to the practice squad.

item.title: Cowboys vs 49ers: 3 causes for concern in Week 10
item.description: The 49ers are an extremely tough matchup for the Cowboys.
item.content:encoded:
After a win over the Indianapolis Colts last Sunday, the Dallas Cowboys face a much tougher task this week, hosting the 7-1 San Francisco 49ers. San Francisco has been, without a doubt, one of, if not the best team in the league nine weeks into the regular season.

The Cowboys have plenty to be worried about in this matchup. With that thought in mind, here are three causes for concern in Week 10.

1) 49ers Rushing Attack

If you don’t stop the run, you are going to have a hard time beating the 49ers. Led by All-Pro Christian McCaffrey, the 49ers have once again been one of the best running teams in football this year. San Fran has recorded 125 or more team rushing yards in five of their eight games and ranks seventh in rushing Y/A (4.6) and third in rush EPA (-0.001), while leading the league in rush success rate (49.5).

One big reason for San Francisco’s success on the ground has been the emergence of rookie running back Kaelon Black. The 49ers spent a third-round pick on Black, hoping he could share the load with McCaffrey and keep the star runner healthy throughout the entire regular season. So far, the plan has worked to perfection.

McCaffrey, who has played in all eight games this season, has scored the second-most (9) rushing touchdowns in the league on just 102 rushing attempts. Both he and Black are averaging 4.5 Y/A with rush success rates of 55% or higher. The duo has worked out about as well as the 49ers could have imagined, and their run game is performing about as well as any in the league. 

If the Cowboys want any chance of staying in this game, their top priority needs to be winning on first and second down and keeping San Francisco’s run game from getting going.

2) San Francisco’s League-Best Run Defense

Another thing the 49ers do better than any team in the league this season is limit the opposing team’s success on the ground. San Francisco leads the league in defensive rush EPA (-0.215) and Y/A allowed (3.3). The 49ers have not given up 100 rushing yards in a game since their Week 2 matchup against the Miami Dolphins, when they surrendered just 102.

The 49ers have been dominant at stopping the run all season, but their last three games in particular have been as good as it gets in that department. San Francisco has allowed an average of just 53 rushing yards over those three games, along with a remarkable –0.290 defensive rush EPA and a 34.9% rush SR.

When the Cowboys’ offense has lacked balance this season, they’ve struggled. It’s going to be extremely hard for Dallas’ offense to play complementary football on Sunday against this San Francisco run defense. If the 49ers continue their trench dominance, it may be a long afternoon for the Cowboys.

3) The Kyle Shanahan Problem

Few people give the Dallas Cowboys more headaches than Kyle Shanahan. The veteran head coach has been a thorn in Dallas’ side for years, with his 49ers dominating the matchup between the two teams for quite some time. 

Shanahan’s 49ers have won four of their last six matchups (including the playoffs) against the Cowboys, averaging 26 points per game. Dallas has not beaten a Shanahan-led 49ers team since December 2020, when they won a fairly meaningless game late in the regular season.

Until we see it happen, it’s hard to have any confidence that the Cowboys can truly compete with Shanahan and the 49ers. Let’s hope the one-sided rivalry flips on its head come Sunday afternoon.

item.title: Saints Rookie Report: Week 10 preview vs. the Panthers
item.description: Two standout performances last week, but the rest of the class disappointed. Hopefully Week 10 can be a bounce back game.
item.content:encoded:
A big game is right around the corner for the New Orleans Saints, and hopefully, after the trade deadline, the rookies can lead the Saints to a win.

WR Jordyn Tyson

It was an exciting debut for Tyson. Yes, he fumbled on his first catch, but it was a really great play by the Browns defender, and Tyson will learn not to reach like that if he is not close enough to the end zone. But after that, when he was able to play, Tyson was open every time he was on the field and picked up some very important yards.

Per head coach Kellen Moore, Tyson will have a larger role in the offense in Week 10, and he could have an incredible performance against the Panthers.

DT Christen Miller

I really do not know what to say anymore. Miller was a healthy scratch on Sunday. I wish there was more clarity on this situation because it makes zero sense why he is not playing. Miller has been a whelming run defender and has made little impact in pass rush, which is perfectly fine. He needs to play more.

Hopefully, after the Davon Godchaux trade, Miller can have more snaps, even if he’s not the starter.

TE Oscar Delp

I hoped that Delp would be more involved in the offense, but that didn’t happen. Maybe if he were the receiver instead of Noah Fant on that drop, the Saints would have scored a touchdown on that play.

The Saints need to start prioritizing the youth on this roster, and I’m hoping Delp can finally get some consistent targets against the Panthers.

OG Jeremiah Wright

News on Cesar Ruiz’s injury has not been released yet, so it’s unknown if Wright is going play, but if he does, good luck to him. The Browns defensive line is very good, and it’s going to be his biggest test yet. He wasn’t horrible against the Steelers, but it was also not good, and he looked like a rookie out there. That’s the expectation, but the Saints will need to see more from him against the Browns.

WR Bryce Lance

It’s time for Lance to be benched and not involved in the offense. He was thrown to once and dropped the ball, which completely stalled the drive and was outperformed by his fellow rookie WRs. Lance is a good blocker, but he’s making consistent mistakes.

WR Barion Brown

Now to Brown; he had a much better day. Like with Tyson, Brown made a really bad mistake that resulted in a fumble, but outside of that, he had a great day. Brown was getting the Saints in great field position on nearly every return and had a 50+ yard catch in this game.

I’m hoping that Brown can take over Lance’s snaps and potentially get a few catches against the Panthers.

RB CJ Donaldson

Donaldson has been injured and is lower on the depth chart now.

OT Mason Murphy

It seems like Kelvin Banks Jr. is on his way back, so Murphy’s chances of starting become even lower.

DB Lorenzo Styles Jr.

As usual, Styles will likely stick with the special teams unit, but it will be interesting to see what happens if Justin Reid gets traded.

item.title: Fantasy Football Rankings: Hayden Winks' WR Blueprint for Week 10
item.description: Fantasy football analyst Hayden Winks lays out the blueprint for the WR position for Week 10.
item.content:encoded:
The Blueprint is my weekly column and basically everything that I use to build out the most accurate rankings I can. There will be this WR column, an RB column and a combination column on the onesie positions. You will find film notes and endless charts. Maybe enough charts to stress test the Yahoo website. I kid.

It's impossible to get every ranking thoroughly early in the week, so be sure to keep checking in on these columns through Sunday morning. As always, my full rankings at every position are available.

1. Jaxon Smith-Njigba (at LV) - 90.5 proj. receiving yards

JSN has played four games with Drew Lock over the past two years, and it's essentially been exactly the same as the other games. He averages 9.5 targets and 106 receiving YPG. Meanwhile, the Raiders have been gashed by downfield targets of late. Jordan Watkins was the WR11 on a deep touchdown, while AD Mitchell (WR3) and Keon Coleman (WR15) also got home with long scores. This is a beautiful spot for JSN.

2. Ja'Marr Chase (vs. PIT) - 89.5 proj. receiving yards

Chase's first half last week was one of the best ever, in terms of all the different ways he can win. He's back to being the WR1 on WR7 usage this month in the league's most pass-heavy offense in neutral situations (66%). The big games will continue, to the point that he'd easily be a top-five overall pick if drafting today.

Chase has faced the Steelers countless times. He's finished as the WR5, WR1, WR5 and WR11 against them since 2024, removing one game with Joe Flacco. Pittsburgh has been excellent against fantasy WRs of late against an easy schedule, but this is a totally different beast. The Bengals have a 26.5-point team total (fifth) as 3.5-point home favorites, and offenses facing the Steelers have the highest neutral pass rate allowed in neutral situations (60%), too.

3. CeeDee Lamb (vs. SF) - 89.5 proj. receiving yards

Lamb dominated without George Pickens last week, bringing him up to WR3 on WR2 usage this season. He's averaging 100.4 receiving YPG, while the Cowboys OL is back to looking dominant.

The 49ers defense has been excellent, and they added a couple of star players of late in DeForest Buckner and Nick Bosa. A game total of 55.5 points is high enough to ignore any defensive stats here, though, especially if CBs Deommodore Lenoir and Renardo Green can't play after not practicing. Dallas has a strong 26.0-point team total (sixth) as field-goal dogs.

4. Amon-Ra St. Brown (vs. NE) - 78.5 proj. receiving yards

It's been a fairly quiet season for St. Brown, who is the WR7 on WR3 usage. He's a positive regression candidate, as he hasn't scored since late September. He still has a 37% target share over the past month despite the forgettable box scores, and the Lions score touchdowns, last time I checked. Good times are coming.

This week brings an enticing draw against a Patriots defense that ranks third in half PPR points allowed to WRs. Star CB Christian Gonzalez will likely see more of Jameson Williams on the boundary than St. Brown on the inside. Malik Washington (WR17), Luther Burden III (WR6) and Omar Cooper Jr. (WR6) are similar players who have played well against them this past month. Detroit enters as 2.5-point home favorites with a 27-point team total (fourth) in Germany.

5. Tee Higgins (vs. PIT) - 76.5 proj. receiving yards

Higgins is the WR4 on WR13 usage this season. He's dunking on everyone and can rack up targets when the Bengals are pushed, as they have the highest neutral pass rate (66%) and are struggling to run the ball in short yardage.

The Steelers have the highest neutral pass rate (60%) allowed on defense, and Higgins has a strong history against them. He's been the WR8, WR15, WR12, WR16, WR9 and WR4 since 2022, removing the lone Week 18 game. That's as good as it gets. Cincinnati enters as 3.5-point home favorites with an implied team total of 26.5 points (fifth).

6. Chris Olave (vs. CAR) - 74.5 proj. receiving yards

Olave came out of the bye with a solid game on 12 targets. The Saints welcomed back LT Kelvin Banks Jr. and introduced first-round WR Jordyn Tyson. Tyler Shough also had another week to rest his fractured left hand. It won't be a surprise if the Saints bounce back after a poor October due to injuries and matchups. Olave is the WR10 on WR7 usage this season.

The Panthers defense has been pathetic of late, while missing EDGE Jaelan Phillips and both of their starting CBs. We'll see if they return here. Olave has battled Carolina throughout his career and won both matchups against it last year, finishing as the WR10 and WR6 with 85-1 and 104-1 lines, respectively. New Orleans is listed as 2.5-point home favorites with an implied total of 25.5 points (seventh). That's probably higher than you thought.

7. Christian Watson (vs. MIN) - 73.5 proj. receiving yards

Watson continues to look like a top-10 NFL WR on tape, and he's produced like that in fantasy (WR5 on WR12 usage). Jordan Love is playing the sport unlike anyone else, and it's been the best TV going this fall.

A matchup with the Vikings will be so entertaining. Watson shredded Minnesota for 147-2 (WR2) back in Week 1, and I'd argue the Packers are better suited to handle this unique defense now than they were before, given the strides the OL has taken. Green Bay has also faced Brian Flores more than anyone else, so it's less of a surprise.

Beyond that, Love has faced the most blitzes and is the QB1 in yards and touchdowns against it, on a QB2 PFF grade. Watson is the WR1 in yards against the blitz himself, and his target share is at 18% without the blitz and 31% against the blitz. That is a very notable gap.

8. Justin Jefferson (at GB) - 77.5 proj. receiving yards

I wrote a ton about Kirk Cousins and Jefferson here.

As for the matchup, Jefferson had his best game of the year against the Packers back in Week 1, finishing as the WR3 with a 92-2 receiving line. Green Bay slowed down the Panthers duo, the Cowboys duo and Amon-Ra St. Brown this month, however. It's a strong defense that is well coached and has the best safety group across the league. I do trust Kirk Cousins to figure it out, assuming he can start right away.

9. Malik Nabers (vs. WAS) - 66.5 proj. receiving yards

Nabers is the WR7 on WR3 usage this month after ramping up in September. He's the WR2 in targets since then and, aside from a dropped touchdown last week, he's been outstanding on tape. J.J. McCarthy has been better than expected and has been willing to launch the ball when in doubt. I still don't trust his play-to-play consistency, but the pass game is largely just Nabers and Isaiah Likely.

The matchup is fantastic with the Commanders struggling in the secondary and placing two DTs on injured reserve. They've allowed the fourth-most passing yards per game (256) on the third-highest neutral pass rate (56%). Washington just let Puka Nacua do whatever he needed last week en route to a WR2 overall finish. Nabers had 121 yards and a score (WR4) against them in Week 5, too. The Giants enter as 2.5-point home favorites carrying a 22-point team total (16th). This is a great spot on paper. I just hope McCarthy doesn't get flustered by the chaos new DC Daronte Jones can bring.

10. Parker Washington (at TEN) - 62.5 proj. receiving yards

Washington's week-to-week swing is very frustrating, but it's not because of his role or play. The Jaguars have simply been blowing teams out to a degree that's kept Washington without the ball late. He's averaging 4.5 targets in the first half (48 YPG) versus 2.4 targets in the second half (13 YPG), solely because the Jaguars are leading in point differential (+108) by a substantial 29 points. Washington can be the reason why Jacksonville is blowing a team out, but if not, then the targets will be forgettable. He's the WR27 in targets per game. Washington is a high-ceiling fantasy WR2.

This is an eruption spot in every way. The Titans have allowed the most fantasy points to WRs (33.0) on the second-most passing yards per game (273). Where they've been lit up the most is underneath and intermediate, where Washington does a bulk of his damage. That'll be an even bigger issue without superstar DT Jeffery Simmons and S Amani Hooker. Jacksonville enters as 10.5-point road favorites with an implied team total of 28.5 points (third).

11. Drake London (vs. KC) - 72.5 proj. receiving yards

London has finished as the WR31 in all Michael Penix Jr. games, aside from the monsoon disaster in Tampa Bay in Week 8. In all career games with Penix, London is averaging 93.4 YPG on 9.8 targets as a clear-cut fantasy WR1. Even during this down month, London has held a 25% target share. I'd buy any hypothetical dip with the Falcons passing significantly more recently, potentially because Brian Robinson Jr. is on injured reserve.

There's no spin-zoning this. The matchup with the Chiefs is terrible if CB1 Mansoor Delane (shoulder) suits up. Even without him, CB2 Nohl Williams is a high-quality player in addition to how well-coached this defense is under DC Steve Spagnuolo. Teams facing Kansas City have the third-lowest neutral pass rate (46%), though they often have to pass more in the final quarter due to game script. The Falcons are 3.5-point home underdogs with an implied total of 21.0 points (18th).

12. Matthew Golden (vs. MIN) - 69.5 proj. receiving yards

Golden reminds me of a young Stefon Diggs. What a talent and just 23 years old without a ton of experience dating back to college and his rookie season. Whew.

The matchup is fascinating with the Vikings. Golden was the WR20 on WR2 usage against them in Week 1, but as I wrote in the Christian Watson blurb, the Packers are better suited to beat the blitz than everyone else. Golden's target share is at 29% against the blitz and without the blitz.

13. Zay Flowers (vs. LAC) - 69.5 proj. receiving yards

It's simply best to throw out the past two games with Joe Fagnano, as Jacoby Brissett is light-years better. As a baseline, Flowers is averaging 12.3 half PPR points and 66 YPG in nine games since last year with Tyler Huntley, who is probably a full tier worse than Brissett himself. Flowers will struggle to get all the way back to the league-leading yards per route metrics that he had in September, but he can sneak back into the fantasy WR1 mix once Brissett gets his feet wet again. It's helpful that the Ravens have first-round LG Vega Ioane and C Cam Jurgens in the lineup. I'm buying the dip.

The matchup with the winless Chargers is strong. They've allowed the fifth-most points against fantasy WRs and were especially shredded by the Texans and Rams over the past two games with S Derwin James on IR. Los Angeles also traded away LB1 Daiyan Henley this week. The Ravens are 4.5-point home favorites with an implied team total of 21.5 points (17th).

14. DJ Moore (at NYJ) - 45.5 proj. receiving yards

Moore has played two normal games to me: Week 1 (WR8 on WR23 usage) and Week 8 (WR13 on WR9 usage). Everything else has been derailed by injury and a matchup with the Vikings' chaotic defense. We're still fully in limbo, but the ceiling is very obvious. I think the type of routes Moore is running suits his skill set best. He's a great fantasy trade deadline target.

This is an eruption spot here. Buffalo is favored on the road as an 8.5-point favorite with an implied team total of 29.5 points (first). The Jets have had a very easy fantasy WR schedule this season, yet have recently allowed WR20, WR8 and WR10 finishes this month to Jalen Nailor, Caleb Douglas and Pop Douglas, respectively.

15. George Pickens (vs. SF)

We'll make sure he plays after missing last week. It's a big-time matchup if he can, with the game total sitting at a wonderful 55.5 points. 49ers CBs Deommodore Lenoir and Renardo Green have not practiced yet.

16. Tetairoa McMillan (at NO) - 66.5 proj. receiving yards

McMillan is averaging 59 YPG with Jalen Coker and 92 YPG without him on 2.0 fewer targets per game, dating back to last year. He's down to WR36 on WR20 usage this month with Coker back in the lineup and Bryce Young coming back to earth behind an injured OL. Hopefully LG Damien Lewis can return here. McMillan is far closer to the WR2/3 border over a big sample.

That said, this matchup is outstanding. The Saints sit 16th in half PPR points allowed per game to WR rooms, but they have been vulnerable downfield by giving up the third-most half PPR points per game on passes over 15 air yards. Did you see the Browns WRs last week? McMillan brings downfield usage with 18 targets over 15 air yards this season, supported by Carolina's top-3 neutral pass rate of 60%. The Panthers are listed as 2.5-point road underdogs with an implied team total of 23 points (12th).

17. Nico Collins (at CLE) - 55.5 proj. receiving yards

Collins not being a full-time player still boggles the mind, but expectations need to be reset in terms of his weekly floor. He's the WR53 on WR50 usage over the past month, even though C.J. Stroud has been playing out of his mind. Collins has averaged a 17% target share on 5.3 targets per game during this bizarre month stretch. The Texans will keep rotating dirty-work Xavier Hutchinson, explosive threat Tank Dell, whatever we're calling Marvin Harrison Jr. and even deep threat Kayshon Boutte. The three saving graces are Collins is amazing, Stroud is firmly a top-10 QB on film and the Texans are now sixth in neutral pass rate since Week 4 when Collins returned.

The Browns are the only defense that plays man coverage at a notable rate. They're talented in the secondary, specifically with CB1 Denzel Ward, but league-wide trends against man coverage lean WR while zone means a higher target share to RBs/TEs. Collins hasn't had the best season against man coverage (1.3 YPRR on 21% targets per route), but he has been amongst the best against it over the past few seasons. Houston heads to Cleveland as 4.5-point road favorites with an implied team total of 22 points (15th).

18. Jameson Williams (vs. NE) - 56.5 proj. receiving yards

The best Jamo advice is to stay within the WR15 and WR25 every week, whether he's played well or not. He's the WR20 on WR33 usage this season, with three games inside the top 12 at the position.

This week's matchup is screaming Yahoo purple after the Patriots were shredded by the Packers' downfield duo last week. Williams will have to do it again with star CB1 Christian Gonzalez in his back pocket. Patriots CB2 Carlton Davis (knee) is out.

19. Garrett Wilson (vs. BUF) - 61.5 proj. receiving yards

Wilson should be back to a full-time role from his concussion this week. His issue is that the entire skill group is healthy now, with both WRs, both TEs and both RBs in the lineup, and there are only so many points available to go around. Over his last four games, Wilson is the WR28 on WR18 usage on a 27% target share. The Jets will run the ball plenty and have struggled to get off the field on the other side of the ball. This season, the Jets' WR room is 24th in usage, averaging 23.1 expected half PPR points. It's harder to make the math work with Omar Cooper Jr. playing well and AD Mitchell getting his own deep/red zone looks.

The Bills DL is pretty good, but their secondary has been a problem beyond CB1 Christian Benford, who has been battling injuries throughout the year. They added S Amani Hooker at the deadline to help out. To date, they've allowed the seventh-most half PPR points to WRs on the sixth-highest neutral pass rate (55%). The Jets are 8.5-point home underdogs carrying an implied team total of 21 points (20th). For what it's worth, Wilson has been the WR60, WR25 and WR2, respectively, against the Bills in his most recent games.

20. Rashee Rice (at ATL) - 54.5 proj. receiving yards

We'll learn more about Xavier Worthy and Josh Downs later in the week.

Just like last week against the Jets, Rice has another great matchup that fits his underneath skill set. The Falcons have allowed the fifth-fewest fantasy points per game on throws under 10 air yards this season, and they just traded away S Jesse Bates. The Chiefs project for 24.75 points (eighth).

21. A.J. Brown (at DET)

Brown is traveling to Germany, and it's not for platelet-rich therapies. Nope, the NFL is sending more teams overseas to play football games. Coach Mike Vrabel said that anyone traveling does not mean they're assured to play. More later.

22. Jalen Coker (at NO) - 46.5 proj. receiving yards

Coker has cooled off. He's only the WR60 on WR45 usage since returning, hauling in just 3.3 receptions per game over the past month. This will likely be his worst stretch of the year based on how good he was in 2025 and before his injury this year. Coker is too good on tape to be this unproductive.

The matchup is a strong one, as Coker can play intermediate and downfield enough to take advantage of where the Saints have been beaten most frequently. New Orleans is allowing the fifth-most passing yards per game (256), and the Panthers are projected for 23.0 points (12th) in a dome environment. Coker had 60-1 against the Saints late last year during his breakout.

23. Germie Bernard (at CIN) - 48.5 proj. receiving yards

Bernard has averaged 7.6 targets per game without Michael Pittman Jr. as the new slot/flanker hybrid. He's the underneath WR, while DK Metcalf runs clear-out routes. Bernard is a post-bye rookie bump candidate now that Aaron Rodgers has welcomed him to the trust tree. Bernard has been the WR26 on WR26 usage this month, racking up WR10 receptions per game.

The matchup with Cincy can be difficult for boundary WRs but CB1 D.J. Turner will be busy with Metcalf, while Bernard gets the easier matchups. The Bengals' LB and S groups have been very poor this year, particularly with tackling and Bernard is not easy to bring down. They've allowed the 10th-most points to WRs in the 5-15 air yards range. A lively 23.0-point team total (14th) as 3.5-point dogs sets Bernard up well.

24. Stefon Diggs (at NYG) - 38.5 proj. receiving yards

Diggs is the WR23 on WR26 usage this year, and his expected half PPR points have bounced between 7.8 and 12.6 in all but one game. Last week's five targets were the season-low outlier, but nothing material has changed. He's the part-time slot-only WR with Antonio Williams, Treylon Burks and Van Jefferson rotating in on the perimeter. Diggs is a step slower this year but remains very crafty and a focal point of OC David Blough's designs in a very mild version of the ARSB role.

One of the biggest NFL stories has been the Giants secondary taking a major leap. They've allowed the third-fewest passing YPG (189), partially because CB1 Deonte Banks has turned into a man-coverage monster. Now, Diggs will be shielded from him while playing inside, but the Commanders only have a 19.5-point team total (22nd) because this defense has stepped up. Diggs didn't suit up for the Week 5 contest against them.

25. Deebo Samuel Sr. (at DAL) - 38.5 proj. receiving yards

We'll learn more about who is playing later in the week, but Samuel was at least a limited participant on Wednesday and Mike Evans is unlikely to play. Samuel should be a part-time player if active, yet he was still fantasy viable in that role before his injury with WR13, WR17, WR61 and WR14 finishes on WR45 usage in September.

The team total sits at 29.5 points (second), and the Cowboys have allowed the third-most fantasy points to WRs on throws under 10 air yards, where Samuel does most of his damage. It's an amazing spot if he can get in a full practice by Friday.

26. Denzel Boston (vs. HOU) - 47.5 proj. receiving yards

Boston is the WR32 on WR27 usage across the entire season. His role will come with volatility, as he's the primary downfield and red-zone threat and those passes are more difficult for bad QBs to complete. The good news is Boston looks like a real deal top-20 WR in the making as a diet-Tee Higgins. The Browns have targeted him the most in second halves, in the red zone and against single high coverage, so being projected to lose is actually good news for Boston.

The Texans have elite edge rushers and good (but volatile) corners. CB2 Kamari Lassiter has been dunked on for a chunk of the season, though some of their leaks in zone have tightened up over the past month. They've still allowed the 10th-most fantasy points to WRs this month and the second-most across the entire season. Houston has allowed the fourth-most points on targets over 15 air yards, where Boston has made many highlight plays. Cleveland has a 17.5-point team total, however, so all of this data needs to be taken with a major grain of salt. Everyone expects Houston to play much better than it has moving forward.

27. KC Concepcion (vs. HOU) - 49.5 proj. receiving yards

Concepcion is up to WR20 on WR31 usage this month after a fairly slow start to his rookie campaign. His juice after the catch is evident and he can stretch the field, even as a slot hybrid player. He reminds me of a young Zay Flowers. Concepcion has been their primary screen player and top target in first halves when coach Todd Monken is most in his bag. There is still no such thing as a floor in this offense, but it wouldn't be surprising if Concepcion leads the team in targets moving forward. He looks like a Round 1 talent to me.

The Texans defense has been better of late, yet still extremely disappointing across the season. I still don't view this as an easy matchup despite all of the production allowed, but where I can be sold is that it's the easiest inside, where SCB Jalen Pitre has been pretty rough and SS Reed Blankenship has been out. Cleveland is slated as a 4.5-point home underdog with an implied team total of 17.5 points (24th).

28. DK Metcalf (at CIN) - 49.5 proj. receiving yards

Metcalf doesn't have a top-10 finish yet. He peaked as the WR12 in Week 6 and has been the WR48 on average, despite being 14th in targets per game. Fourteenth!!! He just hasn't been good in a far more vertical role, with Germie Bernard taking over the underneath role in the slot/flanker spot.

The Bengals have allowed the fewest fantasy points to WRs on throws beyond 15 air yards, where Metcalf is seeing a bulk of his looks. He'll battle elite athlete CB1 DJ Turner, while the rest of his back seven struggles in coverage. Metcalf may be sacrificed here, as he was in Week 3 (31 yards) and last year (49 and 50 yards). The good news is the Steelers project for 23.0 points (14th) as slight dogs in a highly important game.

29. DeMario Douglas (at DET)

We'll see if A.J. Brown is going to play. He's at least traveling with the team. The matchup is clean against the Lions' pass funnel defense either way. Detroit has allowed the most passing YPG (277).

30. Jakobi Meyers (at TEN) - 40.5 proj. receiving yards

Meyers has operated as an efficient complementary weapon in Jacksonville's passing attack. He's the WR45 on WR48 usage this season and his targets have slightly jumped to 5.3 per game over the past month. Jacksonville spreads things out too much for Meyers to be a high-value asset, but he is a red-zone option and can beat up on bad opponents.

He now draws the league's most favorable positional matchup, as Tennessee ranks first in half PPR points allowed per game to wide receivers. The Titans are giving up huge numbers across all depths, ranking first in points allowed to intermediate throws and second to passes under 10 air yards, where Meyers has logged 27 and 13 targets, respectively, this season. The Jaguars are 10.5-point road favorites with a healthy implied team total of 28.5 points (third). There are worse WR3 dart throws during bye weeks and at the peak of injuries.

31. Keenan Allen (at DAL)

We’ll learn about Allen’s availability later on, but the assumption is he plays in a part-time role while he scales up his comfortability with the playbook. He is still a fine underneath defender because of his hands, physicality and understanding of defenses, even if he’s unlikely to spring explosives. The 49ers have a monster team total, and Allen can be effective in the red area. Meanwhile, the Cowboys will be without CB1 Joey Porter Jr. Allen ironically played against Dallas just last week. He drew nine targets (WR21 expected half PPR points), many of them underneath.

On his KNBR radio show, GM John Lynch said 49ers were "focused" on trading for Josh Downs. They were watching Colts film and then Kyle Shanahan said, 'What about Keenan (Allen)?'
"And that started the conversation two and a half weeks ago," Lynch said. "It's a really good fit…

— Vic Tafur (@VicTafur) November 12, 2026

Shakir is Steady Eddie in this awesome Bills offense. He's scored between 7.8 and 11.4 half PPR points in 5 straight games. Over the past month, he's the WR37 on WR37 receptions per game. item.title: Miami Dolphins Vs. Indianapolis Colts: Three Reasons Why
item.description: One has to forge the iron while it is hot.
item.content:encoded:
The 2026 Dolphins have had a tough schedule thus far.  They have only faced 2 teams that currently aren’t in the playoff picture.  One was week 1 against the Raiders when this young team was still wet behind their ears.  The other was a win against their division rival Jets.  They had a lead at halftime against the Pats and kept the most explosive offense in the league in check against the Lions.  That schedule is a tough row to hoe but now gets a bit of a reprieve as they face a team that is actually tanking in the Indianapolis Colts.  Nothing will be easy though, as we will see later.

3 REASONS THE DOLPHINS CAN WIN

THE COLTS OFFENSE IS BAD

The Dolphins have been offensively challenged all season with a regressing OL, rookie WRs, an inexperienced QB that is now on IR, and the loss of their most dynamic threat in De’Von Achane.  That’s a recipe for bad offensive football and for the first few games, it was.  Despite a blip last week against Detroit, they had started to turn things around offensively.  The Colts?  They have no such excuses.  They have one of the best RBs in football with Jonathan Taylor and added pieces like Keenan Allen this offseason to help the receiving unit.  None of it has helped and now they have traded away some of the best weapons they had available.  Both Allen and WR Josh Downs were traded at the deadline.  The WRs left on the active roster are Deion Burks, Ashton Dulin, Anthony Gould, Laquon Treadwell, and former Dolphin Nick Westbrook-Ikhine.  They still have TE Tyler Warren and the Dolphins have struggled with covering opposing TEs since… forever.  But Warren has cooled off from a hot start to his rookie season.  This year, he has only eclipsed 55 yards once and hasn’t found the end zone since week 2.  Overall, the Colts average 4.5 yards per play, which is 2nd worst in the league.  Taylor is still producing with 161 carries, 656 yards, and 8 rushing TDs.  The Colts as a team are 10th in the league is rushing yards with 1037 yards and tied for 4th in rushing TDs with 11.  But that is their entire offense.  QB Daniel Jones is struggling with barely a 60% CP and a miserable 5.7 YPA.  That YPA is tied for worst in the league.  They have 6 passing TDs, tied with Miami and some others for league lowest.  The Dolphins have faced 5 of the top 10 passing offenses in terms of completion percentage, 4 of them in the top 5.  Only the Vikings are in the lower half.  After the Dolphins kept a very good Detroit passing offense under 70%, they can absolutely keep up the momentum against a team that isn’t throwing the ball well at all.  They may allow some underneath completions as Indy has been throwing short.  This is not a scary pass offense at all and with the dearth of WR talent on the roster, Miami’s defense can focus on Taylor and Warren.

THE COLTS DEFENSE IS EQUALLY BAD

In every game this season, the Dolphins have faced a good overall team, a team with a weaker defense but a dominant offense, or a weaker offense with a dominant defense.  This week, the Dolphins get none of the above.  The Colts defense is bad across the board in most metrics.  They are tied for last in yards per play allowed with 6.1.  They allow 362 yards per game.  While there isn’t a ranking for that stat specifically, the Dolphins have allowed 326 yards per game for a comparison.  Their pass defense is middle of the pack in terms of yards per game allowed at 224.8.  Only the Dolphins and Cardinals allow a worst passer rating against than Indy.  They are tied with Miami for 2nd worst in YPA allowed.  They are solid in CP allowed at 61.4% and are tied for 9th in terms of passes defensed with 44.  But they are 2nd to last in INTs with 2 – only the Jets have fewer.  They have 19 sacks on the season, but 4 of those belong to DeForest Buckner, who is now in San Fran.  They are just below Miami in pressure percentage at 21.8%.  In run defense, only the Raiders and Cowboys allow more yards per game than Indy, and only those teams plus the Bengals allow a higher YPC average.  The Dolphins offense struggled against a supposed Lions team, but that defense has started to come together.  Plus, they have a dangerous pass rush and have been good against the run.  The Colts have none of that.  The Dolphins and their run-early-and-often offense should have plenty of opportunities to be effective on the ground.

THE DOLPHINS DEFENSE JUST MAY HAVE TURNED A CORNER

Before the season, I read a tweet that stated Miami would probably have an adjustment period to the defense before it all started to click.  Many times, that can take half the season.  Half the season in and, lo and behold, the Dolphins defense had their best game of the season.  The Lions offense is dangerous, but the Dolphins limited them to nearly 100 yards and 10 points off their season averages.  The pass defense played as well as expected against their weaponry and the run defense, which had been faltering, stepped back up against arguably the league’s best RB.  The pass rush, which was invisible early in the season, has stepped up in recent games with 25 pressures of their season total of 54 coming in the last 3 games. The stage is set for the Dolphins defense to have their signature game and show the development we’ve all been seeing.  Unfortunately for them, they lost stalwart DT Zach Sieler for the season.  However, sophomore Kenneth Grant has been stepping it up since his return from IR.  He played his arguably best game of the season against the Lions and now will be forced to become a bigger part of the DL equation.  The good news is the Colts have traded All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson, and his replacement is rookie Jalen Farmer.  The loss of Sieler will sting more in future games, but the stage is set for Grant and the others to have a solid, if not great, game.

3 REASONS THE DOLPHINS COULD LOSE

ON THE ROAD AGAIN

The Dolphins have not been a team that travels well this season.  I mean, they are 1-7, so there aren’t a lot of positives to draw from overall.  Now, there are some caveats to this.  The 1st 2 games were on the road, and everyone was still in the learning process.  One of those teams is the best NFC team.  They went back on the road in week 4 to face the league’s best defense.  That can skew the stats and make things seem worse than what they are now.  They did get their only win of the season on the road against the Jets.  That said, we know the offense will be limited now.  The defense may have turned a corner, but they allowed the inept Vikings offense to produce 336 yards, which is their 2nd best output this season.  They allowed the Jets to have their 2nd best output of the season.  The fact is that we really don’t know if the Dolphins have truly grown and developed enough that they can go on the road and play at the levels we hope to see.  The Colts, despite their issues, still have a couple dangerous playmakers on both sides of the ball.  The Dolphins need to prove it first.

SPECIAL TEAMS, PENALTIES, AND THE MARGINS

The Dolphins are 31st in average starting field position, starting at their own 28.2.  They are 2nd worst in starting field position allowed, allowing opponents to start at their own 36.7.  That’s nearly an entire set of downs worth of field position on average.  The Dolphins have 13 touchbacks on kickoffs, most in the league and a touchback percentage of 41.9%, the highest in the league.  The next highest is 27.5%.  The Dolphins have committed 71 penalties thus far, with 9 of them having been declined and 1 offsetting.  33 of those are offensive penalties.  They have committed 9 false starts, tied for 9th fewest, but committed 19 holding penalties, 3rd most.  Of the 71 penalties called, 19 of them came on 3rd down and 5 were on 4th down.  That is basically 1 out of every 3 penalties called.  They have 2 penalties for kicking short of the landing zone.  Only 12 teams have done that all season, with Dallas (3) and Chicago (4) have more of those.  Miami is 30th in net yards per punt (39.3), and 26th in FG% (75%).  They allow the 2nd worst yards per punt at 50.1 and 19th in FG% against at 83.3%. It’s stuff like this that can kill any chance for a team to be successful.  Miami can’t continue to give up field position and give the opponent free yardage.  The Colts are almost as bad as the Dolphins in field position allowed for the opponent but are over 2 yards better with their own starting field position.  They are tied for 6th best in penalties called with 54.  They are 8th best in FG% at 91.7%.  These are the little things that for teams like the Colts and Dolphins can be the difference between a win and a loss.  If this game comes down to the margins, the Colts have an advantage.

THE ELEPHANT IN THE ROOM

When I originally drafted this post, Willis had not yet been placed on IR.  I had a section about his health being an issue.  It most definitely is now.  Everyone who was tired of Willis will now get their chance to watch someone else.  And while those fans may have visions of Kyle McCord becoming a superstar dancing in their heads, it is probably going to be anything but.  The league has seen a few rags to riches stories of backup QBs getting a chance to start due to injury and becoming top players in the league; Tom Brady being the penultimate example.  But the most likely outcome is more along the lines of Skyler Thompson, or the plethora of other backups who were… just backups.  This isn’t a “bash Kyle McCord” section by any means.  I hope he DOES become the next version of Brady or Purdy.  But that would not and should not be the expectation.  What IS the expectation is a LOT of checkdowns.  I imagine Malik Washington, Greg Dulcich, and the RBs will get plenty of short, underneath targets.  Perhaps they can get Chris Bell going with some manufactured touches underneath.  Don’t expect to see McCord slinging the ball downfield like a man possessed.  They will keep it very simple and very vanilla.  From a statistical perspective, I would expect that if McCord has a higher CP, that his YPA will be lower.  If he does have a big stat line, it will be from YAC.  If the offense was more experienced, then perhaps we’d see the playbook opened a little more.  But with 3 rookie WRs, young RBs, and a QB that has never taken an NFL snap, expect preseason level offense.  And this is a concern for the Dolphins regarding a chance to win this game.  The Colts are a bad team and with a healthy Willis, I’d expect a double-digit win.  With a hobbled Willis, I’d still expect a win.  With McCord, I don’t know if he can run the offense well enough to even score points.  That’s just a fact of life with the situation.  We can all hope for the best, but the unknown and inexperience factor make this game that SHOULD have been an opportunity for a win, a true toss-up, and very likely a loss.

I SAID WHAT I SAID

On Monday, I really liked this matchup for the Dolphins.  On Tuesday evening, I am less confident in what the Dolphins can do.  The Colts are a bad team that is heading in the wrong direction.  But the Dolphins keep finding new and bigger obstacles to overcome.  The news of Sieler being done plus Willis going on IR really puts a damper on what could have been an exciting week for watching the Dolphins.  The best chance for the Dolphins to get a win is to get Gordon, Allen, and Wright all involved and run the ball a lot.  Like 50+ total rushing attempts a lot.  If the Dolphins have to pass the ball more than a handful of times, we’re looking at 1-8 and probably not another opportunity for a win until week 16 against the Chargers.

item.title: Week 10 Fantasy Football Matchups to Exploit: Parker Washington, Zach Charbonnet, and more players in strong spots
item.description: Ray Garvin takes you through 5 players in smash spots you should definitely have in your fantasy football lineup for Week 10.
item.content:encoded:
Bryce Young's passing volume, DeMario Douglas's turnaround and a Raiders' run defense worth attacking lead this week's lineup targets.

Young is throwing the football nearly 40 times a game. Douglas just produced more receiving yards in two games than he did in his first five. Zach Charbonnet gets a Raiders defense that keeps making opposing running backs look good.

Those are the opportunities I want to chase. These five players sit outside the positional top-10 in half-PPR consensus, but each gives us a reason to get aggressive with a lineup decision. Let's get into where the workload and matchup can pay off.

Bryce Young, QB, Panthers at Saints

Carolina is giving Young enough passing work to make him a serious streaming option. At 38.5 attempts per game through eight starts, he doesn't need every drive to look pretty to help your fantasy team. There are enough throws here to produce a useful afternoon without asking him to become a different quarterback.

Last week against Denver, that volume turned into 276 yards and three touchdowns on 28 completions in 39 attempts. The production can come from different places, too. You don't have to love every Panthers receiver in your lineup to like the quarterback distributing all those opportunities.

New Orleans pressures quarterbacks on 28% of non-blitz dropbacks, ranking 28th, according to Next Gen Stats. That gives Young a chance to work through those passing opportunities against a defense struggling to generate pressure without extra rushers.

His limited rushing production means we're relying on his arm. I'm comfortable with that bet here. Young is a quarterback streamer I'd start this week, with a top-10 finish within reach if the passing touchdowns carry over from Denver.

DeMario Douglas, WR, Patriots vs. Lions

Douglas has earned more consideration than a last-minute desperation play. His recent turnaround is backed by better production and more work per game, and his receiving Trinity score has climbed with it.

Look at the difference. He gained 147 yards on 120 routes over the first five weeks, then produced 287 yards on 112 routes across the next four. His yards per route more than doubled, from 1.23 to 2.56. Trinity moved from 5.81 to 7.16 over those same windows. We're seeing a more productive receiver, with last week's nine targets and 102 yards giving us a fresh example.

Detroit ranks 29th in defensive EPA allowed per play, per Next Gen Stats. That's an opponent I want Douglas getting opportunities against. A.J. Brown remained limited Thursday with ankle and knee issues, so his availability still changes how much work we can expect Douglas to get.

I'm treating Douglas as a WR3 with a path to beating that expectation. If Brown misses again, I'd be even more aggressive about getting him into the flex. Brown's return would tighten the target competition, but Douglas has done enough to deserve consideration either way.

Zach Charbonnet, RB, Seahawks at Raiders

Running backs are averaging 5.21 yards per carry against Las Vegas, the highest rate in the league through Week 9. When a defense is allowing that much rushing production per attempt, I want to know who's getting the carries.

Last week, Charbonnet handled 16 for 77 yards. Jadarian Price finished with nine for 24.

Give me another 15 or 16 carries in this matchup and I'll take my chances. Price is still involved, particularly as a receiver, but Charbonnet can deliver RB2 production from a shared backfield. He just needs Seattle to keep giving him the rushing opportunities we saw last week.

The broader defensive picture supports attacking Las Vegas, too. NGS ranks the Raiders 31st in defensive EPA allowed per play. Seattle's rushing attack has had its own efficiency problems, but this opponent gives it a chance to find more room. Charbonnet is an RB2 I'm comfortable starting.

Parker Washington, WR, Jaguars at Titans

Washington keeps earning targets. Turning them into catches has been the frustrating part.

He drew 20 targets on 75 routes across three appearances during Weeks 6–9. That's a 26.7% target rate, yet he finished with only seven catches for 141 yards. Our receiving Trinity score of 7.11 still places him in the Premium Usage tier. That target access is why I'm sticking with him.

Tennessee offers a chance for the production to catch up. The Titans play 80% zone and rank 27th in pressure without blitzing, according to NGS. StatRankings also shows 63.1% of opposing targets going to wide receivers, fourth-highest in the league. The passing opportunities have tended to reach this position; Washington still has to convert his share.

At WR11 in consensus, he's already being valued aggressively. I like the matchup, but I'd want better receiving conversion before expecting him to outperform that ranking. Jacksonville averaged only 28 pass attempts over those three games, and Jakobi Meyers drew 19 targets to Washington's 20. Meyers returned to limited practice Thursday with his ankle issue, so I'm not treating those competing targets as available work.

Washington stays in my lineup. I'm comfortable chasing the upside of that target access against Tennessee, with a stronger case for an aggressive start if Meyers can't play.

Tank Dell, WR, Texans at Browns

Dell drew a target on 40.9% of his routes last week.

Nine targets on 22 routes? That gets my attention. He turned them into four catches for 105 yards and a touchdown while still playing a partial receiving role. When a player is drawing that much attention on limited routes, I want to consider what a little more playing time could do for his fantasy production.

Now, he gets a Cleveland defense that leads the league in man coverage at 42% and single-high coverage at 73%, per NGS. Dell has averaged 3.2 yards per route against man in the StatRankings split. He's below the qualifying route minimum, so that number is an early indication of success rather than an established strength. The coverage matchup adds interest to the target demand we just saw.

Dell returned to full practice Thursday while dealing with hand and shoulder issues, which is encouraging for his availability. The bigger football question is still how many routes Houston gives him after only two appearances this season.

At WR38 in consensus, I'm willing to chase the upside. Dell is a boom-or-bust flex for a lineup that needs a bigger receiving performance. The route count keeps him out of the dependable-starter category, but another game of strong target demand could make that risk worth taking.

item.title: NFL 2026 Week 10 Start ‘Em Sit ‘Em: Tyler Warren and D.J. Moore are ready to rebound
item.description: DJ Moore and Tyler Warren are both coming off quiet Week 9 showings. Fantasy managers should hold the line and keep starting them in Week 10.
item.content:encoded:
Week 10 is underway and the shootouts just keep coming. With several totals of 50+ on tap, there are plenty of great FLEX and streaming options this week. These are my biggest stands and fades for Sunday's games.

Quarterback

Start: Tyler Shough, Saints

Shough has been in a bit of a slump lately, but a date with the Panthers should turn things around. Carolina is 23rd in EPA per dropback allowed. The game has a sneaky high total of 48.5, the fifth-highest of the week, and the Saints have a 25.5 team total. That’s the seventh-highest mark of the week. With Jordyn Tyson ramping up and Travis Etienne potentially returning, the offense as a whole has more firepower now than at any other point this season.

Start: Patrick Mahomes, Chiefs

Mahomes gets another easy matchup this week. The Falcons look like an okay defense on paper, but most of their success came in the first half of the season. They were 10th in EPA per dropback allowed through five weeks. Atlanta has fallen to 22nd in EPA per dropback over their past five games. That was before trading Jessie Bates to Jacksonville. Vegas is also in on the Chiefs this week with a 25.5 team total.

Sit: Michael Penix, Falcons

The Chiefs are generally a matchup to avoid for quarterbacks. They’re 11th in EPA per dropback and ninth in YPA allowed. Only four teams are giving up fewer fantasy points per game. Penix’s slump is also becoming hard to ignore. After a few bad games, he’s down to 17th in EPA per dropback and a staggering 27th in CPOE.

Sit: Kirk Cousins, Vikings

I’m as excited to see Cousins back in Minnesota as the next guy, unless the next guy works for a sportsbook. The Vikings have a 19.5 team total. That’s lower than the Colts, Jets, and Ravens. A road game in Green Bay is not an ideal spot for Cousins’ homecoming. The Packers are seventh in EPA per dropback and are giving up the seventh-fewest fantasy points to QBs.

Running Back

Start: Blake Corum, Rams

Without Puka Nacua, Davante Adams, Terrance Ferguson, and Jordan Whittington, the Rams have no option other than to run the football until the wheels fall off. Corum’s role was already on the rise before the Nacua (and Whittington) injuries. He had 33 percent of the team’s designed carries—good for 7.6 per game—in his first five appearances. His carry share is up to 44 percent (12 carries per game) over the past month. Corum has also seen half of the team’s goal line carries since Week 7. As 9.5-point favorites over the Cardinals this week, both Kyren Williams and Corum should get going.

Start: Chris Rodriguez, Jaguars

As of Friday morning, we don’t know if Bhayshul Tuten is playing. I expect him to go, but Rodriguez is in a very similar spot to Corum even if Tuten does play. The Jags are 10.5-point favorites at home versus the Titans. No team is expected to blow out their opponents by more. Liam Coen has no issues taking the air out of the football. The Jags have the eighth-lowest PROE this year.

Tuten’s snaps were limited last week, and they will be again if the Jags roll over the Titans. That’s a strong path to a dozen carries for Rodriguez.

Sit: Tony Pollard, Titans

On the other side of this game, the Titans are the biggest underdogs of the week and they get a nightmare matchup for Pollard. The Jags have allowed the second-fewest fantasy points to running backs. They’re a great run defense, ranking third in EPA per attempt, and they also limit rushing volume to an absurd degree. Only the Lions are facing fewer running back carries per game.

Sit: Tyler Allgeier, Cardinals

Allgeier would’ve been a sit whether or not Bam Knight was healthy. The Cardinals have the lowest team total of the week and only the Titans are bigger underdogs. Getting Knight back was the final nail in the coffin. Allgeier and Knight split the backfield in Weeks 6 and 7. Allgeier saw fewer than half of the carries and earned a measly six percent target share. Knight, on the other hand, saw both of the goal line attempts.

Wide Receiver

Start: DJ Moore, Bills

Moore has started and finished four games this year. He has a 27 percent target share and a 44 percent air yards share in those contests. That is alpha WR1 stuff. He turned that into 14.2 PPR points per healthy game, which is in line with Garrett Wilson. The MVP favorite in Josh Allen has a clear No. 1 pass-catcher who puts up good numbers when he finishes games. I’m going to keep playing him until I go broke.

Start: KC Concepcion, Browns

The Browns are finally getting Concepcion more involved on intermediate and downfield shots and it’s already paying dividends. The rookie had an aDOT of 5.2 through five games. He had four targets farther than 10 yards downfield. Concepcion has nine intermediate/deep targets in one fewer game over the past month. His weekly fantasy production has more than doubled since the team started treating him as a real receiver.

Sit: Caleb Douglas, Dolphins

We’re giving our Dolphins pass-catchers a rest this week with Kyle McCord under center. Miami’s -11 PROE was already the lowest in the league. It could reach new lows with the backup QB on the sticks. Unlike most weeks, the Dolphins may actually be in a position to establish their ground game on Sunday. They’re 3.5-point dogs against the Colts this week, which is their second-smallest spread of the year.

Sit: Ladd McConkey, Chargers

The Chargers are scoring the ninth-fewest points per game since 2015, which is already reason enough to bench McConkey. To make things worse, his role isn’t even good. He has seen more than 17 percent of the team’s targets in one game this year. That was all the way back in Week 1. Between his injuries and the team’s struggles on offense, it doesn’t seem like the Bolts are even capable of getting McConkey going.

Tight End

Start: Hunter Henry, Patriots

Henry is in Germany for a date with the Lions that features the third-highest total of the week (50). Detroit is giving up the most fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends. Even after a quiet Week 9 from Greg Dulcich, the Lions are still on pace for the worst seasons of tight end defense of the past 25 years.

Start: Tyler Warren, Colts

Warren will be the entirety of the Colts’ passing attack going forward. Being the only pass-catcher of note in a Daniel Jones offense won’t always be a great experience, but Week 10 is a smash spot for Warren. The Dolphins have allowed the eighth-most catches and the fourth-most fantasy points to tight ends.

Sit: Tucker Kraft, Packers

Kraft is struggling to earn targets with Matthew Golden and Christian Watson both breaking out this year. He has a 16 percent target share and hasn’t run 80 percent of the routes in a game since Week 2. His opponent, the Vikings, do not allow slot or inline receivers to see the football. Minnesota has allowed the fewest targets and the fewest receptions to players lined up in the slot or inline.

Sit: Mark Andrews, Ravens

Jacoby Brissett might save the day for Zay Flowers, but there’s almost nothing to be salvaged with Andrews. He’s averaging a dismal 1.2 yards per route run and is only running a route on 70 percent of Baltimore’s passing plays. Now he gets a Chargers defense that has faced the lowest pass rate in the NFL.

item.title: Seahawks, Broncos, Bengals and Rams stood pat at the NFL Trade Deadline, but what does it mean for fantasy football?
item.description: Fantasy football analyst Chris Allen examines some of the teams who made no moves at the trade deadline, heading into Week 10's main slate.
item.content:encoded:
I'm in the "guide-but-don't-direct" phase of parenting with my 11- and 13-year-old boys. I'll set expectations with a few realistic boundaries, maybe show them how I do things once or twice, and then leave them to it. The results are, well, mixed. Our dishes get "cleaned" with only minimal streaks of grease left behind. The carpets look at least half vacuumed. Maybe if I gave them enough time, they'd get the job done right.

A few NFL contenders had me thinking the same after Tuesday. We all knew what they should do. Other teams even showed them the blueprint for improving at the deadline on their road to the Super Bowl. But some stood pat. I'm sure there were reasons and in January, we'll look back in hindsight and grade both the active and inactive front offices.

However, for now, let's dig into what that means for the skill players stuck in their roles. 

Denver Broncos didn't get their TE

Trades Linked to the Team:

  • Denver tried to acquire Jonathan Taylor but balked at the price

  • The Broncos' front office checked in on Trey McBride

I mean, credit to George Paton for at least making the calls. There's nothing wrong with shopping in the name-brand section of the store. But both interactions signal that head coach Sean Payton wanted to improve both phases of the offense. And not with half measures. Either way, the McBride inquiry hits at a specific part of Bo Nix's game that could use a boost.

Bo Nix to Pat Bryant for a HUGE touchdown pic.twitter.com/OJPPvl48J1

— Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) November 8, 2026

As always, I'll use one rep to highlight a larger point. Check out not just the distance, but the target location on Pat Bryant's (crucial) TD catch in the highlight above. Between the numbers is where passing games live and die. And Nix can create efficient plays in that area of the field with the best of them. But it's just not that often.

  • EPA per Att. to the MoF: 0.35, 9th (out of 31 qualifiers – min. 150 targets)

  • MoF Throw Rate: 44.1%, 26th 

Funnily enough, that's where Trey McBride thrives. He has a 30.7% target rate on throws between the numbers (seventh-most among all pass catchers) with a 2.62 YPRR (ninth-most among all TEs). Theoretically, McBride would've been the ideal complement to Jaylen Waddle, who leads the Broncos when Nix has looked to the middle of the field. But if Waddle's injuries persist through the bye, Pat Bryant (82% route rate, 15% target share), who immediately became one of the top options for Nix, should be on our radar as a depth piece.

Cincinnati Bengals stand behind Joe Burrow

Trades Linked to the Team:

  • I don't want to talk about it.

On top of not completing a trade, my team winds up embarrassing themselves on the national stage. Anyway, the larger point is, despite the urges from media insiders, there were no credible links between an offensive skill player and the Bengals before the deadline. In short, this is the roster that will (hopefully) deliver Joe Burrow his first MVP. But there's still one glaring gap in offense.

Pro: Chase Brown on all 3 inside-5 snaps.
Con: This was his goal line rep last week. pic.twitter.com/M9tXcLqJlt

— Hayden Winks (@HaydenWinks) November 11, 2026

I have Chase Brown on a few rosters, and it's been a rollercoaster. I get excited when the team gets inside the 5-yard line, irate when Brown inevitably runs into a wall and a mix of both when Burrow sneaks it in on the next play. But since Brown doesn't have to worry about Taylor or Tony Pollard coming for his job, there's a path for him to get back into our good graces.

  • Rushing Success Rate: 31.0% (Pre-Bye), 43.8% (Post-Bye)

  • Adj. Yards after Contact per Att.: 2.54, 3.72

  • Yards Before Contact per Att.: 0.9, 1.5

Brown's YPC has been on the rise since Cincinnati came out of its bye (3.5 in Week 7, 4.6 and 6.3). On the one hand, explosives have juiced his per-carry averages (two against the Falcons alone). But last Sunday was his first game with two carries to go for more than 10 yards since Week 3. In addition, even when defenders have met Brown at or behind the LoS, his yards after contact per attempt are up by 41.3%. 

Brown has just one game with a target rate under 10.0%. And before the Bengals turned their trip to Madrid into a blowout, he controlled 63.6% of the backfield totes. As the schedule continues to favor Cincinnati, the fantasy points will come for Chase Brown.

Seahawks leave the offense to Jaxon Smith-Njigba

Trades Linked to the Team:

  • Rumored to have interest in Brian Thomas Jr.

  • Explored a trade for Jonathan Taylor

I understand why Seattle passed on Josh Downs. There'd be too much of an overlap with Jaxon Smith-Njigba. If anything, they need a field stretcher. However, on the bright side, Smith-Njigba remains in the best position to end the season as the Offensive Player of the Year.

Jaxon Smith-Njigba runs his routes with ZERO wasted movement.

Through 8 games, he has 64 REC, 985 YDS and 9 TD.

Back to back OPOY or even MVP? 🤔 https://t.co/s2lafxwoAVpic.twitter.com/G4PVCHHgSH

— Football Performances (@NFLPerformances) November 4, 2026

If Week 18 ended today, Smith-Njigba would have the Triple Crown. He's one of three WRs with a 30+% target rate, and he leads the league in both YPRR and first downs per route run. But the offense could use another gear. I just can't see it coming from any of the remaining WRs.

  • Cooper Kupp: 0.91 (YPRR), 5.73% (1D/RR)

  • Tory Horton: 1.07, 8.41%

Neither Kupp nor Horton offer the downfield element missing from Seattle's passing game. Horton has just three targets of 15+ air yards. Kupp has more targets at or behind the LoS than in the intermediate or deep range. But since Drew Lock is nursing an elbow injury, short-area targets should be in large supply. However, before you try to chase last week's results, a couple of points to keep in mind. 

Drew Lock Strikes Again To AJ Barner, Who Has His Second Touchdown Of The Half.

The Seahawks Keep Finding Him In The End Zone, And He’s Making It Look Easy Out There. pic.twitter.com/UdeRMbzw4u

— SM Highlights (@SMHighlights1) November 8, 2026

AJ Barner has been the Tush-Push option at the goal line and is running routes at the ninth-highest rate among all TEs. But Seattle's PROE fell even further in Zach Charbonnet's second game back (-8.9%, 26th- lowest). Its Week 10 opponent is allowing a league-high 132.1 YPG to enemy rushers. Also, Sam Darnold and Rashid Shaheed should be back out on the field after its Week 11 bye.

As such, if you're looking for any reliable fantasy production out of this offense … better hope you have No. 11 on your roster.

'And with the 13th-overall pick in the 2026 Draft, the Rams select…'

Trades Linked to the Team:

  • Tried to execute a blockbuster trade for Ladd McConkey

  • Called the Browns about Jerry Jeudy

Apologies to the Rams fans for the hindsight jab. And, to be fair, Denzel Boston, Makai Lemon or KC Concepcion alone couldn't cover for the loss of Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. However, being rational doesn't change how L.A.'s receiver corps looks heading into Week 10.

  • Konata Mumpfield: 49% (Route Rate), 6% (Target Share)

  • Tutu Atwell: 48%, 5%

  • Xavier Smith: 49%, 1%

Matthew Stafford has the same problem as Joe Burrow. With two high-end receivers constantly demanding targets, there's less work for the ancillary WRs. All three didn't catch a pass from Stafford until Week 2. But I understand the "next man up" mentality. And, of course, volume is king. With Mumpfield showing out earlier in the season and Atwell liable for an explosive play, both have a place on rosters. However, looking at the schedule, they shouldn't be in any fantasy starter slot unless the situation is dire.

  • Cardinals: 16th (FPPG Allowed), 25th (Success Rate Allowed), 15th (Completion % Allowed)  

  • Packers: 6th, 21st, 11th  

  • Chiefs: 32nd, 4th, 32nd 

Surprisingly, Arizona's defense has given up just one TD to a WR over its past four games. And that's after facing the Seahawks, Cowboys and Rams. The last 100-yard receiver was Malik Nabers in Week 4. The Packers will have DE Micah Parsons back, and the Chiefs are the toughest matchup for opposing WRs.

The Rams' PROE has been below expectations in three of their past four games. TEs and RBs have dominated Stafford's targets in two of them. And the defense is getting healthier. The Packers will be the first true test for the offense to fight back against Jordan Love. But if Adams is back by then, you'll have burned a bench spot on Mumpfield or Atwell for nothing.
