item.title: What awaits Fernando Mendoza in his NFL debut? Facing Seahawks’ No. 1 defense, Raiders remind rookie he’s not ‘Spring Fernando’
item.description: Mendoza’s teammates don’t expect perfection from their new leader under center. They do expect resilience, which their 6.5-point home underdog status suggests they may need.
item.content:encoded:
Fernando Mendoza didn’t “want to talk about myself as a third person.”

But the No. 1 overall pick of the 2026 NFL Draft admitted Wednesday that in the Las Vegas Raiders quarterback room, just that sometimes happens.

Raiders quarterback coach Mike Sullivan looks at his rookie and speaks in the third person.

“In the quarterback room, sometimes Coach Sully, he’ll reference back to ‘Spring Fernando’…” Mendoza told reporters. “It just shows how much improvement there’s been, and I’m a lot more confident.”

“Spring Fernando” had plenty of proverbial skins on the wall, chief among them a Heisman Trophy and a national championship in his lone season at Indiana. But “Spring Fernando” didn’t understand his NFL playbook and teammates as deeply as Mendoza does now, teammates and coaches say. “Spring Fernando” responded differently to blitzes and showed a less advanced command of the huddle; he conceptualized two-minute drills and situational football with less nuance, and he threw the ball less accurately.

None of this, the Raiders say, is a knock on the quarterback whom “you don’t draft him unless you feel that way, taking him first overall,” head coach Klint Kubiak said. But entering an NFL meeting room for the first time can’t compare to observing half a season behind 15-year NFL veteran Kirk Cousins. A first glance at the playbook doesn’t instill concepts as deeply as running the scout team against an NFL defense each week.

So as the Minnesota Vikings approached the Las Vegas Raiders at the trade deadline about acquiring Cousins, the Raiders faced a decision. What was more valuable: letting Mendoza sit a few more games before handing the reins over, or a third-round draft pick and $10 million in salary credit?

“We had to make a hard decision,” general manager John Spytek told reporters. “I mean, we’re all kind of staring the future in the face here with Fernando.”

On Sunday in Las Vegas, Mendoza will receive his first NFL start. The football gods have not gifted him breaks. The Raiders host the Seattle Seahawks, who have allowed the fewest yards per game in the NFL through nine weeks. Only three defenses across the league have allowed fewer points. Adding to the chess match nuances, as well as the heightened emotions: Kubiak will be scheming against the team whose offense he coordinated to the Super Bowl nine months prior. Play-callers will know each other intimately. Kubiak hopes Mendoza does not feel pressure rests on his shoulders alone.

“We have an awareness of his situation and being in his first game,” Kubiak said. “However, we’re not peeling back anything and we’re going to go do what the whole team does best, all 11. … 

“He’s got to do his job and not worry about a whole lot else. Everybody does their 1/11th, and everything around him elevates their play.”

Raiders’ best bet is taking pressure off Mendoza. But are they capable? 

When the 2016 NFL season kicked off, the Dallas Cowboys arrived at the “Sunday Night Football” opener with a rookie quarterback. 

Incumbent starter Tony Romo had fractured a bone in his back during a preseason game, after second-string quarterback Kellen Moore broke his ankle during training camp. So the Cowboys’ fourth-round pick got the start. Dak Prescott completed 25 of 45 pass attempts for 227 yards, no touchdowns and no turnovers as the Cowboys lost 20-19 to the New York Giants.

Dallas would go on to win its next 11 games and 13 overall en route to the NFC's No. 1 seed. Along the way, the Cowboys decided their recipe: Don’t ask Prescott to air it out and play hero ball in every moment. 

Fast forward to Mendoza, and former Cowboys head coach Jason Garrett recommends a similar strategy.

“You try to take the burden off of him…” Garrett, now on NBC’s “Football Night in America” studio show, said Wednesday on a conference call. “Quiet the game down for him, try to get the running game going early, high-percentage throws early, move the quarterback. Try to get him to be 5-for-5 [passing] before he even thinks about it to get into the flow of the game. Those aren’t easy things to do, but that has to be your objective.

“Once he gets his legs underneath him and he’s got a good look in his eye, then you start trying to attack the defense a little bit more.”

Mendoza has some traits playing in his favor for that proposed game plan. He was highly accurate last year in college, completing 72% of his pass attempts even as he led all FBS passers averaging 10.78 air yards per attempt. The 23-year-old Mendoza is more mobile than his 38-year-old predecessor. And the Raiders, who rank fifth in passing through nine weeks under Cousins, have a handful of reliable targets in the passing game — beginning with tight end Brock Bowers (whose alignments more often position him like a receiver than an in-line tight end) and receiver Tre Tucker. The Raiders' offensive line has also pass-protected well, ranking second in pass-block win rate, per ESPN’s advanced metric.

Working against Mendoza: the rest of his Raiders surrounding cast and his first opponent. While Mendoza, Kubiak and the locker room emphasized players stepping up to share the load with Mendoza, Cousins was disproportionately carrying the team until he got traded. While Cousins ranked fifth in passing yards and 11th in passer rating, the Raiders’ run game has languished with the second-fewest rushing yards per game (71.3) and the fewest rushing yards per attempt (2.89). The Raiders' defense hasn’t alleviated the offense’s load: No team has allowed more points than the Raiders’ 29.8 per game, and no team has allowed more yards per game than the Raiders’ 385.4.

Las Vegas has won four games overwhelmingly because of its passing game — and now faces Seattle’s No. 1-ranked defense and No. 1 passing defense for Mendoza’s first outing. When the Seahawks shuttered the Kansas City Chiefs’ otherwise explosive run game last month, Patrick Mahomes and Co. managed just 3 points.

Multiple former offensive play-callers cautioned against translating that into a pass-happy plan.

“You want [his pass attempts] to be in the 20 to 25 [range],” one former NFL play-caller told Yahoo Sports on condition of anonymity. “You don't want the kid to go out there in his first-ever game against the Seattle defense and throw the ball 43 times.”

Early discipline matters, Garrett said.

“If you try to go after these guys too early, then you get a lot of negativity happening for the quarterback in the first start of his career [and] it can be tough sledding,” Garrett said. “Get him settled. It’s OK to punt early. But take the burden off him and get him comfortable.”

Raiders on transition from Cousins: Not ‘punting on this season’

Mendoza’s teammates don’t expect perfection from their new leader under center. They do expect resilience, which their 6.5-point home underdog status suggests they may need.

“Everyone has faith in him,” Bowers said. “You might have a bad play here and there, but you just got to flush it. And I know he does a good job at that.”

In two initial college seasons at Cal, Mendoza completed 66.5% of his pass attempts for 4,712 yards, 30 touchdowns and 16 interceptions. In his third year, at Indiana, that rose to 72% of passes for 3,535 yards, 41 touchdowns and just six interceptions. No one in FBS football last year passed for more than Mendoza’s 41 touchdowns and no one was more efficient than his 182.9 rating.

But a national championship moment caught his current teammates’ eyes as much as Mendoza’s accuracy and precision.

Facing fourth-and-4 with 9:18 to play against Miami, Mendoza tucked the ball and ran upfield for a 12-yard touchdown.

FERNANDO. MENDOZA.

THE PLAY OF A LIFETIME ‼️ pic.twitter.com/g3o5nNNslr

— ESPN (@espn) January 20, 2026

“He lowered his shoulder and ran through the guy for a touchdown,” Tucker said. “So that shows the kind of guy we're getting and we're very excited about that. … 

“When I put it to him, I feel like there's nothing that he can't do.”

Mendoza’s preseason play was up-and-down as he completed 25-of-45 pass attempts for 240 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions while taking four sacks.

How will he look with the Raiders’ starting lineup after running the scout-team offense in recent months?

“I haven't really got too much reps with him, but just whenever they're pulling up tape or whatever, he's just making great throws over and over,” running back Ashton Jeanty said. “Accurate, precise, going through his reads. So giving the defense a good look week in and week out over there.”

Spytek praised Mendoza this week as having “passed every test,” insisting the Raiders’ trade of Cousins “in no way signifies that we are punting on this season.”

But perhaps the Raiders will measure progress in the coming weeks based not only off game results but also on the development of a young core individually and in concert. How will Kubiak’s impressive play-calling look with his new quarterback? Will teammates step up to rally around Mendoza?

No one expects a mistake-free rest of the season.

But one NFC talent evaluator who scouted Mendoza in the preseason pointed to his 35 college starts and 1,008 college pass attempts as indications that Mendoza may transition smoothly.

“These older prospects that have seen a lot of ball, I feel once they start acclimating to the speed of the game, can take off quickly,” the evaluator told Yahoo Sports. “I wouldn’t be surprised to see him do really well.”

item.title: Lions vs. Patriots: 3 key matchups for Week 10
item.description: Our Detroit Lions vs. New England Patriots preview identifies three key matchups.
item.content:encoded:
It’s Germany week as the Detroit Lions (6-2) travel abroad to take on the New England Patriots (5-4). Buckle up. It is about to be a wild 11-day gauntlet as the Lions play the Patriots, Tampa Bay Buccaneers, and the Chicago Bears in that span.

Meanwhile, the NFC North is absolutely insane. I love it.

This is how it was always meant to be. This is adversity.

Turn on local Detroit radio, and you’ll likely hear voices of doubt and concern. Switch to national outlets, and you’ll hear the Bears declared the favorites in the NFC, Jordan Love MVP discourse, and Kirk Cousins transforming the Vikings’ outlook as contenders.

I love it. This is how it was always meant to be.

With a win on Sunday, the Lions will take over the top spot in the NFC North with the Chicago Bears on their bye. In that event, the Lions will be 7-2 and 2-0 in the division, whereas the Bears will also be 7-2, but 0-2 in the division. All signs point to an absolute battle on Thanksgiving, as Ford Field will undoubtedly, again, welcome Ben Johnson with echoing boos.

But first, taking care of business against the Patriots and Buccaneers is priority one.

Three key matchups. Three opportunities to control the division.

Blake Miller vs. Gabe Jacas

The first key matchup is rookie versus rookie. New England’s second-round pick, EDGE rusher Gabe Jacas, Illinois, has been a disruptive playmaker from the start. For Grit Index followers, his name is not new. Jacas was one of the guys we were pounding the table for here, leading all EDGE rushers with a 9.14 Grit Index score. The Lions went with Derrick Moore, to my surprise. But an uncertain knee injury for Jacas became known after the draft process that may have been one of the contributing factors for the Lions to favor Moore.

Jacas’ early play has been impressive both as a pass rusher as well as a run defender.

He plays violently with a relentless motor.

On the other side, however, the Lions have had a strong start from right tackle Blake Miller, who has had more ups than downs in his rookie campaign. Last week, however, was notably more down than his average performance.

When Jacas is lines up over Miller, my eyes will be on how the Lions’ rookie tackle responds. It will be an entertaining matchup, for sure, but also the winner of it will have a say in which team has a better flight back across the Atlantic.

Christian Mahogany vs. Christian Mahogany

The next matchup is all between the ears for left guard Christian Mahogany. After a benching for breaking team rules last week, Mahogany is back in the starting lineup. It became apparent watching the game against the Miami Dolphins that the Lions’ best five along the offensive line includes Mahogany, as Miles Frazier’s struggles impacted the Lions’ typically potent offense.

“Look, if you say you’re gonna do something, you better hold up to it, otherwise you’re gonna lose respect of the people around you,” said Dan Campbell on 97.1 The Ticket. “Because if I’m sitting in that seat and I say one thing and then I don’t do it, I would immediately lose respect for that person. So we stick by what we say we’re gonna do here.”

It is time for Mahogany to take the next step as a professional. He knows it.

The time is now. If not now, Dan Campbell surely will not let one player hold the rest of the team back.

Patriots’ rookie cornerbacks vs. Lions receiving corps

With veteran cornerback Carlton Davis III already ruled out for the game, the Patriots will be leaning on two rookies to play the role opposite Christian Gonzalez. The two rookies are fifth-round pick Karon Prunty, Wake Forest, and undrafted free agent Channing Canada, TCU.

Following up on an abysmal performance against the Green Bay Packers’ paper tiger deep passing attack, the New England secondary will face an even more difficult matchup against the Lions. Following Jared Goff’s first game of the season without a passing touchdown and back-to-back games with an interception, ending his early-season streaks, Goff will be looking to right the ship against the Patriots. If I were a betting man, an Amon-Ra St. Brown anytime touchdown in his home country of Germany may be the safest bet of the weekend.

Three key matchups. Three opportunities.

Drei Schlüsselduelle. Drei Gelegenheiten. (Thank you, Google Translate).

item.title: Fantasy Football Week 10 Fades and Busts: Tony Pollard's hot streak gets extinguished
item.description: Fantasy football analyst Matt Okada sheds light on players we should temper expectations for in Week 10.
item.content:encoded:
Welcome to the 10th of 17 weekly articles spotlighting the fantasy fades of the week! I am your host, Matt Okada, and I'll be bringing you half a dozen potential busts each and every Friday, from now until fantasy championships.

As a note, just because a player earns a "fade" or "bust" designation doesn't automatically mean they should be benched — it depends on the rest of your roster or the options on your waiver wire. But you can expect them to fall short of expectations (when I get them right). I include a "What to Do" section for every player to help with that.

Without further ado, here is my list for Week 10 of the 2026 season.

QB Matthew Stafford, Los Angeles Rams at Arizona Cardinals

Things have fallen apart quickly for Matthew Stafford and the Rams offense with the loss of Davante Adams late in Week 6 and the loss of Puka Nacua late last Sunday. The reigning MVP has not finished higher than QB12 in any week without Adams this season, and roughly half of his yards and touchdowns have gone to those two wide receivers in combination. Starting in Week 10, he'll be playing with both receivers absent for the first time since early 2024, when he averaged 8.5 fantasy points per contest over a four-game stretch, with just two touchdowns and three interceptions.

Without Adams' ability to separate, particularly in the red zone, or Nacua's ability to create tough catches and yards out of thin air, Stafford is left with very few reliable options moving forward (no disrespect to Tutu Atwell and Konata Mumpfield). After consecutive outings with fewer than 13 fantasy points — including just 12.22 points against an extremely soft Commanders defense — it's hard to imagine him being more productive without Nacua, regardless of matchup. So while the Cardinals are probably "bright green" against quarterbacks in your fantasy app, I fear Stafford is a trap this week and I would look to stream a QB instead.

What to do ❓ Don't play Stafford (outside of 2QB leagues) if you can find any reasonable streaming alternative. That includes names like Tyler Shough, Bryce Young and C.J. Stroud (whom I actually love as a QB1 moving forward).

RB Ashton Jeanty, Las Vegas Raiders vs. Seattle Seahawks

On one hand, this feels bold. Fade Ashton Jeanty, a second-round fantasy pick who's been the RB17 in points per game? On the other hand, it also feels expected, following the trend of Jeanty's season into a matchup with the Seahawks. From Week 1 through Week 8, Jeanty's carry count stayed equal or dropped lower every single successive game and, when it bumped back up for the first time in Week 9, it was from two carries to six.

Since Week 5, he's tied for 51st among running backs in carries per game (with Corey Kiner) and 64th in rushing yards per game (behind, unironically, Sione Vaki). Jeanty’s producing the entirety of his dwindling fantasy value through receiving, with at least three catches in every outing, 35+ receiving yards in seven of nine games and three of his four touchdowns coming through the air. Unfortunately, everything gets tougher against the Seattle defense, especially with a rookie quarterback in Fernando Mendoza making his debut start. Vegas is tied for the second-lowest implied total on the week (17 points) behind only the Cardinals (the other team with a rookie QB debut against a tough defense), and the 'Hawks are allowing the eighth-fewest receiving yards per game to running backs.

Even if Jeanty manages six or seven catches for 50 to 60 yards, he's still on a collision course with single-digit fantasy points. It's hard to sit him, I get it, but it was hard to sit Derrick Henry last week on TNF — and that was the right move.

What to do ❓ Jeanty slides out of RB2 range for me this week, so if you have decent depth and can turn to backs like Zach Charbonnet, Blake Corum, Woody Marks (if healthy) or even Corey Kiner ... strongly consider it.

RB Tony Pollard, Tennessee Titans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars

I have to imagine that Pollard's 62.2 fantasy points in his last two games entering this week are the most for any player to crack this column in its history. Yes, he was revelatory in Weeks 7 and 8 against the Browns and Bengals. He averaged 5.4 yards per carry and scored five touchdowns in those two weeks, for 1.15 fantasy points per opportunity. But let's exercise some prudence here. Through the first six weeks, Pollard had logged just 4.0 yards per carry, scored just one touchdown and averaged 0.47 points per opportunity, dead last among qualified players. Can we really trust that drastic of a two-week breakout for the 29-year-old running back in the Titans offense?

I'm hesitant ... especially this week against Jacksonville. Entering the trade deadline, the Jaguars had allowed the second-fewest fantasy points per game to running backs (15.3), with just 68.3 rushing yards per game (also second-fewest) and just four touchdowns in eight games. Then, they significantly strengthened their defense with the acquisitions of DTs Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux and safety Jessie Bates III. One of the other teams tied with the Raiders for second-lowest implied total this week is, unsurprisingly, the Titans. That's even worse for Pollard than it was for Jeanty, and I think the Tennessee RB comes crashing back down to earth this Sunday.

What to do ❓ You'll likely see Pollard projected and ranked quite highly around the industry ... I've got him right in Jeanty's range in half-PPR (outside the top 24), which means you can pivot to the same group of names mentioned above.

WR DK Metcalf, Pittsburgh Steelers at Cincinnati Bengals

Frankly, DK Metcalf has been one of the most annoying and unpredictable calls in all of fantasy from week to week this season. He's hit double-digit fantasy points three times — just barely in Week 3, thanks to a touchdown — but fewer than seven points in every other game. His best performances came against the Browns and Buccaneers, theoretically tougher matchups for receivers, and then in the rematch with the Browns, he caught one pass for four yards. A big part of the problem is that he sees significant target volume but is usually horribly inefficient with that volume. He's one of 16 wideouts averaging 8+ targets per game but has scored just 7.7 fantasy points per game on those targets ... while every other receiver on that list has averaged 10+ PPG.

His 51.6% catch rate and 5.9 yards per target are both dead last on that list as well, and his 0.94 fantasy points per target is the lowest among 64 wideouts with more than 30 targets this season. At this point, I'm convinced the inefficiency is the expectation for Metcalf, rather than an opportunity for a breakout. He'll likely see solid volume against the Bengals — although he only had five targets in their first meeting — but the way he's played so far in 2026, he needs double-digit targets to approach double-digit fantasy points. I'd prefer a player with a higher floor, even on fewer expected opportunities.

What to do ❓ Metcalf is sort of the Jeanty of wide receivers — he slides out of WR2 range for me this week and I'd prefer "streamier" plays like Jalen Coker, DeMario Douglas, Omar Cooper Jr. or either Browns rookie.

WR Tre Tucker, Las Vegas Raiders vs. Seattle Seahawks

Tre Tucker has done just enough, just often enough, to keep himself in the fantasy starter conversation week to week this season. That ride includes 18+ fantasy points in three games … but it also includes fewer than eight fantasy points in the other six games, including a doughnut two weeks ago against the Jets. And in Week 10, that ride will be as bumpy as it gets. Not only are the Raiders starting rookie Fernando Mendoza in his NFL debut — after trading a productive Kirk Cousins at the deadline — but they're doing it against the Seahawks. Seattle's defense has allowed the fewest fantasy points per game to wide receivers in 2026, with a league-low 99.6 receiving yards per contest and 6.2 yards per target.

They've also been particularly tough against downfield throws — where Tucker sees the vast majority of his targets — allowing the lowest yards per target, catch rate, success rate and EPA per play on those throws. And, unsurprisingly, they've surrendered the lowest explosive pass rate in the league, at just 10.1%. Nothing about this game instills confidence in Tucker and his occasional shot at a big fantasy day — barring a lucky breakaway play, expect another game with fewer than eight fantasy points.

What to do ❓ Tucker is already a volatile FLEX option week-to-week, but between Mendoza and the Seahawks secondary, he's outside the top-40 wide receivers and should not crack any reasonable redraft (or DFS) lineup.

TE Tucker Kraft, Green Bay Packers vs. Minnesota Vikings

Last week, I tagged Dalton Kincaid as the tight end fade against Minnesota and he ended up with just 4.3 fantasy points on three catches on Monday Night Football. While Tucker Kraft might feel like a slightly better tight end in a vacuum, he's also extremely risky against this Vikings defense. They've allowed just 3.9 receptions and 7.4 fantasy points per game to tight ends, both the fewest in the league, with just one touchdown in eight games. The 57.4% catch rate they've surrendered to the position isn't just the lowest in the league this season; it's the lowest for any defense in any of the last four seasons.

It also doesn't inspire confidence that Kraft is coming off his worst game of the year, with just one catch against the Patriots, a game in which he accounted for just an 11% target share and 0.3% of Jordan Love's 372 passing yards. And while Kraft's 8.0 points against this unit in Week 1 are actually the second-most by any tight end they've faced, no one has yet hit double digits and strong options like Sam LaPorta (5.0) and Colston Loveland (0.8) have been busts in this matchup as well.

It's hard to sit a regular TE1 in fantasy, but Kraft is on the absolute fringe this week.

What to do ❓ The most reasonable "streaming" name you can confidently start over Kraft is Hunter Henry — whom I love against the Lions — but if you happen to have someone like Kincaid, Brenton Strange or possibly even Darren Waller, give it some thought.

item.title: Eagles News: Nick Sirianni’s job security among top storylines to monitor the rest of this season
item.description: Philadelphia Eagles news and links for 11/13/26.
item.content:encoded:
Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation!

How are you feeling about Nick Sirianni right now? Do you think he deserves a mulligan? I don’t think it’s accurate to frame it as one bad season when the losing dates back to the second half of last year (5-12 in their last 17 games). If the Eagles lose 15 straight to finish the season at 2-15 (not the most likely outcome but hardly impossible), I think it’s pretty difficult to justify bringing Sirianni back. Or if it’s not far off from that final record. If the Eagles bounce back in the second half, you have to wonder how much that should be valued. The 2011 Eagles won their final four games to get to 8-8 … only for that “momentum” to prove useless for the 2012 Eagles, who finished 4-12.

Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links …

Six storylines to watch during the rest of a lost Eagles season – Inquirer

The coaching staff. Nick Sirianni wouldn’t rule out coaching changes after the game Sunday, but he did say a day later that no changes have been made. “Right now, like I said earlier, we’re going through our self-scout process,” he said. “Guys are working on studies right now and we’re determined to figure things out and get on the right track, and that’s what we’re worried about right this particular time.” That wasn’t a ringing endorsement of Mannion staying in his current role. Could the Eagles make a change at play-caller as soon as this week? Could they move on from offensive line coach Chris Kuper? The self-scouting process won’t be kind to either coach. If Mannion remains in his position for the rest of the season, it’ll be worth watching if the offense can show signs of life, with Joe Milton or whoever is taking snaps at quarterback. There’s also the Sirianni of it all. Will Jeffrey Lurie and Howie Roseman think injuries and a flawed roster outweigh the rest of the problems and decide to keep him? Is there a number of consecutive losses that warrant an in-season firing?

NFL Power Rankings: Week 10 Edition – BGN

29 – Philadelphia Eagles (LW: 29) – After starting the season 2-0, the Eagles have lost seven straight. It couldn’t be more obvious that Nick Sirianni has no answers. The good news is that Howie Roseman is doing his part to put the team in a position to rebound beyond this season. The Jordan Davis trade was an absolute heist.

5 Questions About Jordan Davis: Jaguars Got ‘A Good Vibes Addition’ – Big Cat Country

The Jacksonville Jaguars have traded for Jordan Davis! To learn more about Duval’s newest defensive tackle, we went straight to the source. Here are 5 Questions with Brandon Lee Gowton, who covered Davis’ time with the Philadelphia Eagles over the past four and a half seasons for SB Nation’s Bleeding Green Nation.

International player Joshua Weru on his development behind the scenes – NBCSP

Joshua Weru was the talk of training camp this summer. While draft pick Uar Bernard grabbed headlines this spring, it was the Eagles’ other International Player Pathway Program player who began to stand out in August. The edge rusher from Kenya flashed in practices and even in the preseason a bit — to the point where some worried he’d be claimed if the Eagles dared to waive him to get him to the practice squad. But that was months ago and now we’re in November. Weru has spent all season on the Eagles’ practice squad. And most days this season, Weru walks through the Eagles locker room mostly unnoticed. He’ll sit at his locker without being bothered and hadn’t really been asked for an interview all season. Until last week. So Weru seemed a bit surprised when he was approached and asked for a few minutes, which he graciously handed over. What have the last couple of months been like? “It’s been good,” Weru said. “I continue to say I’m so lucky to be here. The amount of reps we get on scout team and developmental have been good. Just seeing things better and recognizing blocks quicker. Just getting my strike stronger. Even though I’m not necessarily getting stronger in the weight room, like actual game strength is getting slightly better. Just those things because you’re more used to doing certain movements so you’re getting better at it.”

2026 Midseason All-Pro Team: Joe Burrow, Penei Sewell, Dexter Lawrence and more – PFF

Linebacker: Ventrell Miller, Jacksonville Jaguars. Miller has arguably been the breakout player of the NFL season, with his 92.6 overall PFF grade leading all linebackers. He has impressed in coverage, earning a 91.3 PFF coverage grade and recording four pass breakups, and he has also been strong against the run, with an 84.7 PFF run-defense grade that ranks fourth at the position. Second Team: Zack Baun, Philadelphia Eagles.

Zach Ertz surprises Julie Ertz with National Soccer Hall of Fame selection – PhiladelphiaEagles.com

First year of eligibility for the National Soccer Hall of Fame? No problem for Julie Ertz, one of the best midfielders and defenders in the history of the United States Women’s National Team. Amongst many other accolades, the two-time World Cup Champion, two-time Concacaf Women’s Championship winner, and two-time U.S. Soccer Female Player of the Year was surprised with the news that she would be inducted into the Hall of Fame by her husband, Eagles tight end Zach Ertz. “(The National Soccer Hall of Fame) reached out to me about two months ago to try and figure out the best way to do it,” Zach Ertz said after the surprise. “I kind of was out of ideas, but I wanted to get the family together, not in the craziness of the house, and make it a little special.”

Jameis Winston tried everything to draw the Commanders offsides – SB Nation

That’s right, you heard that correctly. After using an old-school cadence right out of youth football (Hut 1, Hu2 2), Winston turned to the lyrics from “Who Let the Dogs Out,” which won a Grammy award back in 2001 for the Best New Dance Recording. Winston’s effort did not have the same level of success, and the Giants were forced to take a timeout before punting the ball away.

Giants try to keep perspective, but this was a massive missed opportunity – Big Blue View

You wanted them to, of course. Did you really think, though, that the New York Giants were just going to waltz to the NFC East title without things getting interesting? The Giants made things interesting, and much more convoluted, by losing to the Washington Commanders on Thursday and missing an opportunity to take firm control of the division. The 5-3-1 Giants are still in first place, and will remain there through the weekend no matter how the second-place Dallas Cowboys fare on Sunday when they host the 7-1 San Francisco 49ers. Their path to a first division title since the 2011 Super Bowl season is now much more difficult, and uncertain. If the Cowboys can upset the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday, they will be 5-5, just 1.5 games behind the Giants with eight weeks left in the season. The Commanders are now 3-5-1, and with a tiebreaker advantage over the Giants should also feel like their season is very much alive.

Commanders help Cowboys’ NFC East hopes with TNF win over Giants – Blogging The Boys

The NFC East just became a tiny bit easier for the Dallas Cowboys. They owe the Washington Commanders big time. On Thursday night there was an NFC East tilt that went down to the wire. When it looked like the New York Giants (5-3-1) were going to take a serious step forward, a leap to be honest, in the NFC East race, Jayden Daniels hit Stefon Diggs to give Washington the late lead that held until the end. In case you are unaware, a Giants win on Thursday night would have just about sealed the NFC East race. Nothing is ever official obviously, but it would have given them six wins to date and with the tie from their previous matchup against Washington that would have put them at 6.5 in an effective sense.

Cowboys’ Porter: My absence is because of injury, not my contract – ESPN

Dallas Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr. wants it known that his absence from the field the past two weeks has everything to do with an ankle injury and nothing to do with him worrying about a future contract. “I don’t even know where that narrative come from,” Porter said. “I get it. It’s the internet, but I really don’t pay no attention to that or really care for that. My goal is to win games and play football, and that’s what I want to do. So if there’s any chance I could get on the field, I’m going to get on the field and do what I do best.” Porter was inactive last week on the road against the Indianapolis Colts and was unable to finish the loss to the Arizona Cardinals because of an ankle injury he initially suffered Oct. 4 against the Houston Texans in his first game with the Cowboys following the trade from the Pittsburgh Steelers. On Thursday, Porter did not practice for the second straight day, but he worked on the resistance cords during the portion of practice open to the media Thursday. He said he did some running and felt confident.

Key takeaways from Washington Commanders win vs. Giants in NFL Week 10 – Hogs Haven

The Commanders minced no words when discussing the importance of Thursday night’s game against the New York Giants. It was a must-win for Washington. Jayden Daniels said it. K’Lavon Chaisson, too. Dan Quinn avoided the phrase but emphasized Thursday’s importance time and again. While that sounds like a reach with nearly half Washington’s season left to play, it’s shockingly fair. The win put the Commanders in the mix and within striking distance of the Giants, who lead a weak NFC East by a little bit. A loss would have put Washington four back with eight to play, a virtually insurmountable lead to block a path to the postseason. The Commanders lit their margin of error on fire in the early going of the regular season, with one blown opportunity after another. Washington simply had to win this one. The Commanders were able to do that in stunning fashion. The Daronte Jones defense came up huge in the fourth quarter, and the Commanders finally surged ahead to secure a 24-21 victory over the Giants at MetLife Stadium.

Commanders-Giants on ‘Thursday Night Football’: What We Learned from Washington’s 24-21 win – NFL.com

Time doesn’t run out on Commanders. Five weeks prior, Jayden Daniels and the Commanders bungled a seemingly sure win and settled for a tie against the Giants. Trailing by four points on Thursday night with eight minutes to play, Daniels threw his first two interceptions of the season on back-to-back drives. Having struggled over the past two years to pull out wins of any kind, but having squandered one-score verdicts aplenty, Daniels and Co. seemed destined for another late-game collapse. The defense stepped up, though, and so did Daniels with one more chance. Jump-started by a controversial defensive pass interference call drawn by Treylon Burks, Daniels found Stefon Diggs over the middle and the veteran turned it into a 32-yard, game-winning touchdown. In an otherworldly rookie season in which Daniels captained the Commanders to the NFC Championship Game, there was a magical feel and magical outcomes. Remember the Hail Mary versus the Bears? (I do). During Daniels’ rookie year, Washington was 8-4 in one-score games. Since, it’s gone 4-8-1, with that fourth win coming Thursday. It was a game in which Daniels was almost certainly targeting Diggs on a 1-yard TD pass to Ben Sinnott with 5 seconds to go in the first half. Sinnott had one catch on the season before catching four for 42 yards and the TD in this one, thanks largely to Chigoziem Okonkwo missing much of the game dealing with a back injury. Daniels completed 23 of his 33 pass attempts for 249 yards, three touchdowns and two picks after his first 207 passes of the season went without a single INT. For the first time in a long time, Daniels and the Commanders provided a bit of a charmed feel. With the triumph, the Commanders now have a 19% playoff probability as they sit in third place in the NFC East at 3-5-1. However, at 1-0-1 against the first-place Giants (5-3-1), they hold the tiebreaker. Odds are slim that Washington will punch a postseason ticket, but time didn’t run out on Thursday. Daniels and the Commanders have that at the very least.

item.title: Broncos have no comment as to Jim Harbaugh's complaints about Daiyan Henley trade
item.description: The failed Daiyan Henley trade has exposed a previously unknown (by many) loophole in the trade deadline, which could be used by an unscrupulous team to leverage better terms after a deal is otherwise done — and the time for negotiating trades has otherwise ended.
item.content:encoded:
The failed Daiyan Henley trade has exposed a previously unknown (by many) loophole in the trade deadline, which could be used by an unscrupulous team to leverage better terms after a deal is otherwise done — and the time for negotiating trades has otherwise ended.

Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh essentially accused the Broncos of being unscrupulous by taking the position that Henley had failed his physical but that the physical would magically be un-failed if the compensation for Henley was reduced from a fourth-round pick and a fifth-round pick.

In response to an inquiry from PFT, the Broncos had no comment on the situation.

During a normal week, Broncos coach Sean Payton would be meeting with reporters on Friday. Because Denver has a Week 10 bye, Payton won't speak to the media again until Monday.

At that point, it will be interesting to see whether he shares the Broncos' position, or whether he makes it clear that Denver is moving on.

Of course, that doesn't stop the Broncos from pushing their position on an off-the-record basis to one of the reporters who routinely covers the team. And their position seems to be that the Broncos believe the Chargers weren't candid about the condition of Henley's knee during the discussions that preceded the trade.

The Broncos also contend, not on the record (yet), that the goal was to acquire Henley (who is in the last year of his contract) not as a rental but as a long-term addition. (They would have acquired exclusive negotiating rights with Henley through the opening of the legal tampering period in March.)

Still, with Harbaugh making his case on the record, the Broncos should do the same. While there's surely some sensitivity to the impact of the chatter about Henley's knee on his future earning potential, the options (in our view) should be to address the situation on the record or say nothing.

Through it all, the more important point is that the league's procedures allow things like this to happen. And, apparently, deadline deals have indeed been tweaked in the past based on concerns about a player's physical.

It shouldn't be that way. For any deal done before 4:00 p.m. ET on the day the trade window closes, there should be two possible outcomes: The player passes the physical and the deal goes through as negotiated, or the player fails the physical and the player reverts to his prior team.

item.title: Bills Mafia’s Week 10 rooting guide: Let’s make that AFC lead a little bigger
item.description: The Bills are sitting atop the AFC. Here's who needs to win — and lose — to help Buffalo build its lead in Week 10.
item.content:encoded:
That was some kind of ugly beautiful. 

I’m not sure what we watched for the first hour of Monday Night Football, but I’m glad we got back to our regularly scheduled programming before halftime. 

That’s when the NFL’s No. 1 offense shifted gears and dared the NFL’s No. 1 defense to keep up. They couldn’t. Not because the Buffalo Bills were playing with the gas pedal down, but because Josh Allen and Co. were flipping the script. Let the pass rush in, and James Cook gets out. Then Josh Allen gets out. And just when it looked like the Minnesota Vikings might have things figured out, the Bills changed it up again. 

Was it glorious? Nope. But it was brilliant, and somehow, by the fourth quarter, the stress level of Bills Mafia was actually down. And when does that ever happen? 

Anyway, when Kyle Allen (yep, Josh got to sit out the entire victory formation so he didn’t accidentally drop back below that 5,000-yard rushing mark) took the final knee, the Bills were on top. 

Of the Vikings. Of the AFC East. Of the AFC. Heck, of the whole league. 

Yes, you read that right. Buffalo is currently the NFL’s top team. But all that really matters to us right now is the AFC playoff picture and what needs to happen for the Bills to keep their grip on the conference’s No. 1 seed and force everyone else to make a trip to the icy tundra of Western New York in January. 

So, let’s take a look at who Bills fans should be rooting for this week. 

_____________________________________________________________________________ 

  1. Buffalo Bills (7-1) 
  1. Denver Broncos (7-2) 
  1. Jacksonville Jaguars (6-2) 
  1. Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2) 
  1. Kansas City Chiefs (6-2) 
  1. Cincinnati Bengals (6-2) 
  1. New England Patriots (5-4) 
  1. Cleveland Browns (5-4) 
  1. Las Vegas Raiders (4-5) 
  1. Baltimore Ravens (4-5) 
  1. Houston Texans (3-5) 
  1. New York Jets (2-7) 
  1. Indianapolis Colts (2-7) 
  1. Miami Dolphins (1-7) 
  1. Tennessee Titans (1-7) 
  1. Los Angeles Chargers (0-8) 

_____________________________________________________________________________ 

AFC East 

Buffalo Bills at New York Jets 
Root for: Bills 

You don’t need me to tell you why, but here it is anyway. The Bills control their own destiny from here until they lose. And the longer they put that next loss off (I mean, none of us here are going to complain if it doesn’t happen until next August, right?), the less effect it will have on the standings. As long as they keep winning, it doesn’t matter what anyone else does. Go Bills! 

New England Patriots at Detroit Lions 
Root for: Lions 

The Patriots are still Buffalo’s closest competition in the AFC East, and they’re heading to Munich with a 5-4 record and one of those wins came at Buffalo’s expense. A loss to Detroit would give the Bills a little more breathing room in the East, and we certainly aren’t going to complain about that.  

Miami Dolphins at Indianapolis Colts 
Root for: Colts 

Miami isn’t exactly threatening Buffalo’s division lead at 1-7, but there’s no reason to give the Dolphins anything to celebrate. Indianapolis is sitting at 2-7, so neither team is making much noise in the AFC playoff race. We’ll take a Colts win and another Miami loss, thank you very much. 

_____________________________________________________________________________ 

Rest of the AFC 

Houston Texans at Cleveland Browns 
Root for: Texans 

A Houston win would give Buffalo a little help in the strength-of-victory department while moving the Texans a little farther away from the top of next year’s draft. Neither is a bad thing for the Bills. But if Cleveland wins, we won’t complain too much. A Browns win, paired with a Patriots loss, could knock New England out of the playoff picture, at least for now. So, either way, there’s a little something in it for Buffalo. 

Pittsburgh Steelers at Cincinnati Bengals 
Root for: Steelers 

Both teams are sitting at 6-2, so somebody has to get that third loss. And looking at the remaining schedules, we’d rather it be Cincinnati. The Bengals have Kansas City and then a bunch of teams sitting below .500 on their schedule, while Pittsburgh still has to face Denver, Jacksonville, and Baltimore twice (and the Ravens are always a threat for a late-season rebound). There are plenty of opportunities for the Steelers to pick up a few losses down the stretch. Let’s give Cincinnati its third one now and worry about Pittsburgh later. 

Kansas City Chiefs at Atlanta Falcons 
Root for: Falcons 

Kansas City is sitting at 6-2, just behind Denver in the AFC West and still very much in the hunt for the conference’s No. 1 seed. A loss to Atlanta would give Buffalo a little more breathing room and maybe take some of the stress out of that Thanksgiving night showdown between the Bills and Chiefs. Besides, do we really need an excuse to root against Kansas City? 

Jacksonville Jaguars at Tennessee Titans 
Root for: Titans 

Jacksonville is sitting at 6-2 and currently holds the AFC South lead. That’s a little too close to Buffalo for comfort. Tennessee, meanwhile, has managed just one win all season, and now that Buffalo owns the Titans’ fifth-round pick in the 2027 draft, we don’t need them getting too win-happy. But knocking Jacksonville down a notch in the AFC standings is worth more than a few spots in the fifth round. Titan Up! 

Seattle Seahawks at Las Vegas Raiders 
Root for: Seahawks 

The Raiders are sitting at 4-5, outside the playoff picture but not completely out of the race. Seattle is an NFC team, so a Seahawks win keeps Las Vegas from gaining any ground in the AFC without helping another conference contender. A Raider win would help the Bills’ strength of victory, but right now we aren’t playing for ties.  

Los Angeles Chargers at Baltimore Ravens 
Root for: Chargers 

The Chargers haven’t won a game all season, and we’d certainly appreciate it if they decided to start now. Baltimore is sitting at 4-5, and while the Ravens are floundering around right now, Lamar Jackson is promising to return to the field soon. We’d prefer he didn’t have much of a playoff race left to return to. Another Baltimore loss would make that climb even harder. Plus, a winless team knocking off the Ravens on Monday night? We’d happily watch that.  

_____________________________________________________________________________  

NFC Rooting Interests 

  • Minnesota Vikings over Green Bay Packers – Strength of Victory 
  • Los Angeles Rams over Arizona Cardinals – Strength of Victory 

Games that don’t move the needle for Buffalo: 

  • San Francisco 49ers at Dallas Cowboys 
  • Washington Commanders at New York Giants 

_____________________________________________________________________________  

Teams on Bye 

Chicago Bears, Denver Broncos, Philadelphia Eagles, Tampa Bay Buccaneers 

_____________________________________________________________________________ 

If the football gods are feeling generous this weekend, the Bills could wake up Monday morning with a little more room to breathe at the top of the AFC. Denver and Pittsburgh would still be close enough to make things interesting, but Kansas City and Jacksonville would need binoculars to see Buffalo two full games ahead of them. And the Patriots? Three and a half games back sounds like a lovely place for them to be. 

Of course, none of those favors mean a thing if the Bills don’t handle business against the Jets. So, let’s beat New York, enjoy a little scoreboard watching, and see just how much separation we can put between the Bills and everyone chasing them.  

Go Bills!

item.title: Carolina Panthers 2026 fan mailbag: Injuries, blame for losses, early look at free agency, and more!
item.description: Answering all your questions in this week’s fan mailbag!
item.content:encoded:
Hello CSR! Welcome to Brian Answers, part two of your weekly Panthers fan mailbag for everyone! I think all the fans are looking for answers following a 3 game skid, I’m here to try and give you those. Let’s dive in!

TXPanther: Which of these guys would be priority for designated to return from IR? Would you save any spots? They have used 2 designations so far which leaves 6 to be used.

Well, the Panthers answered that question this week by activating RB Jonathon Brooks, CB Mike Jackson, WR Xavier Legette, and OL Brady Christensen (last week on that one). Those would have been my choices, and I expect one of the remaining spots is earmarked for Jaycee Horn unless they feel he cannot return. I have a feeling they’ll have used up all of their IR to return designations before the seasons end, sadly. Only one I’m not entirely sure about is Xavier Legette, but hopefully he comes out and shows us some of the promise that made him a first round pick.

@WTMealey: rank these in order of who you feel is too blame for losses or put another way what change would give the most results

Injuries

Evero

Lack of talent on the roster-feel free to point fingers

Canales

Bryce

Morgan

Tepper

I don’t really feel I can put it in a particular order, but I blame Ejiro Evero and Dave Canales mostly for the unpreparedness of the players and the lack of discipline on bone headed penalty plays. Obviously, injuries certainly play a role since the Panthers have been very snake bitten by them. I know Bryce Young hasn’t played in the out of his mind way he did to start the year every game, but I’m still not going to blame him for the majority of the Panthers losses.

storybook: Would you rather win the division at 8-9 again or have a better draft pick?

I’m still of the mindset that you should try to make the playoffs. This fan base really enjoyed the playoff game last season and that’s really the point of all of this right? Get into the dance, see what happens. I also trust this front office to make good decisions no matter where they are picking in the first round, so having a better draft pick doesn’t give me as much anxiety as it did in the past.

GooseCreek: The Panthers will have 25 free agents (13 offense/11 defense/1 special teams) at season’s end (3 ERFA* & 22 UFA** players). ERFA players (B. Tremayne, C. Bullock, & TeRah Edwards) are routinely tendered leaving 22 players (11 offensive/10 defensive/1 spec. teams) for resolution. I suspect the team allows J.J. Jansen (special teams) to decide his own fate (return?/retire?).

My question to you, Brian: Who makes your priority list in each of the following categories?

Three (3) Offensive players to retain? Three (3) Offensive players to let walk?

Three (3) Defensive players to retain? Three (3) Defensive players to let walk?

Any practice squad players you would seek to retain under a Futures contract?

*ERFA: Exclusive Rights Free Agents **UFA: Unrestricted Free Agents

  • I think at this point you look to retain OT Ikem Ekwonu. Rasheed Walker isn’t the answer and you probably need to have Monroe Freeling playing one of the tackle spots since I suspect Taylor Moton won’t be around next season. I also think you retain TE Tommy Tremble if his contract demands are relatively reasonable, which they should be. Finally, I think you hold onto WR Brycen Tremayne, who has been very good for the Panthers when called upon and is excellent on special teams. You can probably let C Luke Fortner walk since he hasn’t been good and should be looking for a replacement. The rest of their free agents on offense are fairly retainable but not priorities in my opinion, Brady Christensen may change this answer depending on how he looks in action.
  • I think you have to retain CB Mike Jackson, even despite his injury. The Panthers still need 3 starter level corners and they won’t have a need (when healthy) if they bring him back to pair with Horn and Will Lee III. I think you also have to retain LB Bobby Okereke after his performance as a guy they signed off roster cuts. And of course, you gotta retain the Ace That Runs The Place 2.0, Nick Scott. The rest of their list doesn’t feel like people I’d worry too much about if they walk.
  • I’d say WR Ja’Seem Reed, CB Corey Thornton, and CB Marco Wilson. Beyond that I really have no idea on some of these guys.

SmoothC: What head coaching jobs will be available by season’s end?

My guess would be the Eagles, Ravens, Chargers, Buccaneers, and maybe the Cowboys. I hope not for Carolina, but time will tell.

Senanima: How long does Waller sip the youth giving Kool Aid?

Probably at least two more seasons. He’s a pretty specialized player and doesn’t have as much mileage for an NFL player at his age as you’d expect. Might make sense to bring him back again in 2027.

Highmiles: We all know injuries have killed us this year. The question is why are we more injury prone than most teams? Bad trainers and conditioning coaches? Poor draft selections? By this I mean trying to draft better players that drop in the draft due to injury history. Turf field?

I’ve never been a fan of the turf field regardless of what the NFL points to as “statistics” correlating to the injuries on turf vs grass. I’ve played on both and can tell you turf definitely seemed to feel like it did more damage. I don’t blame the coaches or staff for it, the Panthers just seem to have bad luck especially this season. And as far as draft selections go, you can really only point to Jonathon Brooks, and I still feel like his issues were mostly just bad luck. I think you can make an argument his first injury after entering the league MIGHT have been a coaching/staff oversight by playing him too fast, but they’ve given him more than enough rehab time since then. Sometimes injuries just happen and there are many players’ careers that fizzled out more due to bad luck than anything. I’m hoping he gets a chance to show off on his return stint this year.

positivebob: Was Morgan right to stand pat at the trade deadline or should he have moved a high value player, Derrick Brown? for draft capital? Or was he handcuffed by having less than 1 mil in cap space, until todays restructure of Moton’s contract? That still only freed up less than 4 mil.

I think this is a great question. The Panthers have been in a weird spot where they looked like they could (and still can) compete for a playoff spot, but their roster isn’t one where you can trade for a guy or two and make a run like other teams. The Panthers are also not actively rebuilding and have been in the “talent collection” stage if that makes sense. Letting Derrick Brown go is a move that basically signals the season is over, and wholesale changes are coming in the off-season. I think Dan Morgan was right to just stand pat, this team doesn’t need to be blown up again right now.

Slick22: How many activations from IR do we have left?

They appear to have 2 left following this week. 2 more if they somehow make the playoffs.

That’s all for this week, Panthers fans! Join us next week for another edition of the weekly mailbag!

item.title: Our Offense vs. Their Defense: Carolina Panthers
item.description: The Saints offense could get its rhythm as reinforcements make their way back
item.content:encoded:
The New Orleans Saints’ offense will look to build off what was a solid outing against the Browns. The great news for the Saints is that they seem to be getting healthier at the right time. The Saints have an offense that ranks 19th in total yards, averaging 325 yards per game; 15th in scoring, averaging 23.1 points per game; 26th in rushing, averaging 95.3 yards per game; and 14th in passing, averaging 230 yards per game. The Saints are actually one of the best teams on third down, converting 43.5% of their attempts, which ranks seventh in the NFL.

This offense will be facing off against one of the weaker defenses in the league in the Carolina Panthers. The Panthers bring a defense that ranks below the Saints’ offense in nearly all of the aforementioned categories, except for passing yards allowed. The Panthers are allowing only 211 passing yards per game, which ranks ninth in the NFL.

The area the Saints should look to attack in this game will be the running game. The Saints do not necessarily have an advantage in this area, but the Panthers are so bad at defending the run that this could be a situation where the Saints’ weakness turns into a strength. The Saints are expecting to get RB Travis Etienne Jr. back from injury, and pairing Etienne Jr. with Audric Estime may give this offense the running back duo it has been searching for since the start of the season.

Carolina does not give up a lot of explosive passing plays. The Panthers are actually tied with Seattle for the fewest in the NFL, having allowed only 18. Because of how proficient their passing defense is, the Saints will need to complement the running game with a strategic passing attack that allows them to complete passes in the short and intermediate levels of the defense, forcing the Panthers’ safeties to start playing closer to the line of scrimmage.

The Saints have had offensive line issues all season, and those issues could be more prevalent on Sunday, as starting center Erik McCoy will be unavailable due to a biceps injury he suffered against the Browns last week. Missing McCoy for this game could be a big loss, but getting Etienne Jr. back could almost feel like an even trade.

If the Saints can run the ball with the same level of effectiveness they had against the Browns, it will help keep the Panthers’ pass rush in check. The Panthers have only 12 sacks so far this season, so neutralizing their pass rush could help make this offense more effective and potentially set the Saints up for one of their more complete performances of the season.

The Panthers’ defense is not that good, but the Saints’ offense has been very inconsistent. If the Saints can score early, keep the offense balanced, and protect the football, they should leave the Dome as the No. 1 team in the NFC South on Sunday afternoon.

How do you think the Saints will match up against this Panthers defense? Do you think the Saints can become the No. 1 team in the NFC South?

Share your thoughts in the comments.

item.title: Seahawks reveal their 2026 Midseason Honors
item.description: Who did the team give Offensive and Defensive MVP to? What about best plays of the season so far?
item.content:encoded:
The Seattle Seahawks have announced their 2026 Midseason Honors. The honors at stake include: Offensive MVP, Defensive MVP, Special Teams MVP, Top Newcomer, Best Relief Performance, Best Play on Offense, Best Play on Defense, Best Play on Special Teams, Trent to Continue, and Thing to Clean Up. Let’s see who and what items won each honor. 

Offensive MVP: Jaxon Smith-Njigba 

To nobody’s surprise, the offensive MVP midway through the season is JSN. He is a front runner for his second NFL Offensive Player of the Year Award, and frankly could be a finalist for the MVP this season as well. Through nine games, JSN has 71 catches for 1,036 yards and nine touchdowns. If he were to keep up this pace for 17 games, that would put him at 134 catches for 1,957 yards and 17 touchdowns. Not only would these numbers break each Seahawk single-season receiving record, they also would put JSN as:

  •  the second most receiving yards in an NFL single season (Calvin Johnson is first with 1,964 yards); 
  • the seventh most receptions in an NFL season (Michael Thomas is first with 149 receptions); and 
  • tie for the sixth most receiving touchdowns in an NFL season (Randy Moss is first with 23 receiving touchdowns)

All of these numbers make it safe to say that JSN is your offensive, and frankly team MVP midway through the 2026 season. 

Defense MVP: Ernest Jones IV

On defense, choosing an MVP may be a little more difficult. There are multiple candidates who could take this honor. Byron Murphy II, Leonard Williams, Demarcus Lawrence, Devon Witherspoon, Nick Emmawori, Julian Love, the list continues. The defensive performance for Seattle is really a testament to how close knit this team is and how dialed in Mike Macdonald has them. All of that being said, the Seahawks gave this honor to the green dot himself, Ernest Jones IV. 

Jones IV is the leader of this defense, and a critical backbone to the number one defense for yards/game in the NFL. Jones IV leads the team in tackles (88), which is good for fourth most tackles in the NFL. Jones IV also has three sacks (tied for second most on the team), five passes defensed (second most on the team), and has one interception. 

Special Teams MVP: Michael Dickson

For anyone watching Seahawks games, a huge piece of the team’s success comes from their All-Pro punter who makes pinning the opposing team’s offense inside their own ten-yard line look easy. Dickson has a 42.8 net average this season, and has 15 punts inside the 20 with only two touchbacks. Thanks to Dickson’s toolbelt of different kicks, Seattle has been able to get two turnovers off of muffed punts, and only allowed eight returns for 39 yards all season long. 

Top newcomer: Emanuel Wilson

Entering the 2026 season the Seahawks only had a few newcomers outside of the draft. The biggest names included Emanuel Wilson, Dante Fowler Jr., Rodney Thomas II, and Trevon Diggs. Considering the last two are currently on the practice squad, and Fowler Jr. only got his first sack this last week against the Arizona Cardinals, it makes this honor a little easier to give. 

That shouldn’t be taken as a knock on Wilson, however. The Seahawks running game has struggled mightily throughout the 2026 season, thanks to injuries. However, the one player who helped keep the boat afloat was Wilson. Despite his noticeable lack of speed and agility, Wilson was still able to deliver big blows to defenders with his physical running style. This bruising ability really helped Seattle run the ball late in games. Take for example, Wilson was able to seal the victory over the Arizona Cardinals in week two with 92 rushing yards. Wilson was also able to show this ability in his 100-yard game against the Kansas City Chiefs in week 7. Wilson currently leads the team in rushing yards (403) and rushing touchdowns (3). 

Best relief performance: Drew Lock

The Seahawks have enjoyed multiple great relief performances, such as Rodney Thomas II filling in for the injury-marred safety room early in the season, and recently with Josh Jones filling in for left tackle Charles Cross. However, the most important position in football still is the quarterback. 

Lock is currently undefeated on the season, beating the New England Patriots in Week 1, and beating the Arizona Cardinals in Weeks 2 and 8. In these three games, Lock has completed 71.1 percent of his passes, for 597 yards, five touchdowns and zero turnovers. Lock has a 116.0 passer rating. This passer rating would lead the NFL if he had enough attempts to qualify. 

The way Lock is performing has created a quarterback controversy in some fan’s eyes. Although it will be shocking to see the Seahawks start Lock over a healthy Sam Darnold, it will be interesting to see how each quarterback plays the rest of the season. Lock’s contract expires after 2026, could he perform well enough to make John Schneider consider keeping him over Darnold into 2027? 

Best Play on offense: Drew Lock to Jaxon Smith-Njigba vs. Arizona

The Seahawks best play on offense goes to their longest scrimmage play of the season, an 82-yard touchdown from Lock to JSN. This huge touchdown happened on the second play from scrimmage in the week two victory over the Arizona Cardinals and essentially ended the game for Arizona just as it began. This early lead allowed Emanuel Wilson and the run game to take over and keep the Cardinals out of arms reach for the rest of the game. 

Best Play on defense: Nick Emmanwori pressures Patrick Mahomes into Ty Okada interception

The game against the Kansas City Chiefs felt a lot closer than the final score would lead you to believe. At one point in the game when the Chiefs were driving (potentially to tie or go up on the Seahawks’ 3-0 lead), Nick Emmanwori, lined up as a linebacker, used his elite closing speed to hit quarterback Patrick Mahomes and force him into an errant pass that was intercepted by safety Ty Okada. 

Although this play itself was very impressive, this honor felt like a way for the Seahawks to give an honor to Nick Emmanwori as well. And who can blame them? Emmanwori has been an elite chess piece for Mike Macdonald. His performance against the Chiefs may have been the most impressive performance of the star safety’s young career. 

Best Play on Special Teams: Michael Dickson and Nehemiah Pritchett team up to create a turnover vs. 49ers

With the Seahawks having no return touchdowns this season, it makes sense to give this honor to a forced turnover made by the Special teams. As mentioned above, Michael Dickson has forced two turnovers with his various styles of kicks. In the week 5 loss to the 49ers, Dickson created one of these turnovers against 49ers returner Jacob Cowing. Cowing muffed the catch and when attempting to recover his muff was thumped by Nehemiah Pritchett, allowing Eric Saubert to recover the ball.

Although this is an impressive play by Dickson, Pritchett, and Saubert, it will be disappointing if the team cannot improve on this play later this season. With Rashid Shaheed returning from injury soon, it will be interesting to see if he can house a return to the house. Or perhaps Tory Horton, or Jadarian Price can assist in housing a return as well. 

Trend to Continue: Overall strong play on defense

This Seahawks team would arguably be nowhere without their defensive performance all season long (no disrespect to MVP candidate, JSN). Seahawks.com does a great job at lining up all of the defensive stats below: 

“Through nine games, the Seahawks rank first in total defense (244.2 yards per game) and passing defense (155.1), second in opponent yards per carry average (3.4), fourth in rushing yards allowed (89.1), tied for fifth in takeaways (13) and fourth in scoring defense (18.0) despite that number being inflated by opponents scoring two defensive touchdowns against Seattle and setting up several other scores with short fields on takeaways.”

The other impressive thing to note with the Seahawks’ defensive performances is the fact that they are doing this with injuries hitting them all season long. Early in the season, the Seahawks were without starting safeties Julian Love and Ty Okada. And more recently the team has been without defensive linemen Uchenna Nwosu and Leonard Williams. These injuries have not appeared to impact the team’s defensive performance, as the next wave of the 70 man roster have been able to keep Mike Macdonald’s unit as elite as can be. 

Thing to clean up: Turnovers

Although the run game as a whole could be considered for this honor, the honor has to go to overall turnovers. In the Seahawks’s four losses, they have committed 11 turnovers. Many of these are unfortunately due to Sam Darnold, who is tied for fourth most interceptions in the NFL despite missing two (three if you count week 1) games. Darnold is not alone in the turnover issues however. The Seahawks running backs have also fumbled the ball five times (Emanuel Wilson twice, Jadarian Price twice, and George Holani once). Rashid Shaheed also coughed the ball up once as well.

If the Seahawks want to get into the playoffs and defend their Super Bowl title, cleaning up the turnovers is a must.

item.description: Jackson needed surgery to repair a broken and dislocated thumb suffered in Week 8 against the Bills.
item.content:encoded:
Lamar Jackson could miss anywhere between six-to-10 weeks as he recovers from a broken and dislocated thumb suffered against the Buffalo Bills in Week 8, head coach Jesse Minter said in a statement on Friday.

Jackson "is doing everything he can" to return this season after undergoing surgery, Minter said, as the 4-5 Ravens continue to battle in a tight AFC North.

"Lamar is doing well as he recovers from the broken and dislocated thumb injury he suffered in Week 8," Minter said.

"Recovery timelines are challenging to predict, but injuries like this that require surgery typically take about 6-10 weeks to heal. He is doing everything he can to get back, and we will let his progress guide the timing of his return.

"We are committed to playing our best football over the second half of the season."

Jackson, who had been out since Week 4 with an ankle injury, suffered the injury during his first pass in Week 8, making contact with the hand of Bills linebacker Gregory Rousseau. The quarterback left the game immediately and did not return. He was placed on injured reserve later that week with the hope that he could return later this season.

The Ravens have eight games remaining in the regular season and still have their bye week awaiting them in Week 13. A six-to-10 week recovery timeline certainly allows for Jackson, who reportedly told teammates to "just stay alive," to return this season. But that could also depend on where the team is in the AFC playoff hunt when he's approaching 100% healthy and ready to play.

With backup Tyler Huntley on season-ending IR with turf toe, the Ravens turned to Joe Fagnano as QB1 after Jackson's injury. The Ravens went and acquired Jacoby Brissett last week from the Arizona Cardinals. He is expected to start on Monday night against the Los Angeles Chargers.
