item.title: The 2026 season is somehow worse than the 2011 Colts
item.description: The long-term outlook might be as bad as it’s been for the Colts.
item.content:encoded:
Ah, 2011. To be young again. Fifteen years have passed since then and a thousand things have changed in the NFL. History doesn’t repeat itself, but it sure does rhyme. The 2026 season for the Colts is starting to look and feel a lot like that disastrous 2011 season when Peyton Manning missed the entire year. Somehow, some way, though, it might actually be worse.

Let’s go back to where it all started. Kerry Collins was brought in off the street and proceeded to get lit up to open the season in Houston. Curtis Painter and Dan Orlovsky took it from there and produced a 2-14 season after an 0-13 start. Manning, Saturday, Clark, Addai, Garçon, Diem, Brackett, and many others were gone by 2012. It marked one of the darkest times in Colts franchise history.

As dark as that season was, 2026 said, “Hold my beer.” You see, in 2012, the Colts were able to draft Andrew Luck. Remember? 2011 was the “Suck for Luck” year. There was an incredible consolation prize for being so bad. 2026? Well, it may not be as awful from a record or even on-the-field talent perspective, but it actually looks worse. 

Key players like Buckner, Nelson, and Downs are gone already. The departure of more names is sure to follow. Unlike the 2011 team, there is no positive mantra to pull the team through. There is no Luck coming to resurrect them. Heck, there isn’t even a first-round pick. That is what makes this year worse. It’s not about 2026 itself. It’s about the long-term effects. The future is murky. After 2011, there was a direction and goal during the season. This season sees the Colts treading water, or worse, drowning. Many more questions linger over the Colts now than in 2011. To make it worse, the answers aren’t as clear either.

2011 was a gut punch for a fanbase that was used to high-level winning. Watching Manning and others walk out the door was enough to make a grown man cry. There was hope and a direction forward, though. This year, 2026? What are we working towards? Where is the hope? What is the future? A stockpile of draft picks and Jonathan Taylor is about all there is to be excited for. From “Suck for Luck” to “Sucks to Suck,” 2026 seems to be worse than the worst Colts season in recent memory.

item.title: Falcons ink CB C.J. Henderson to new two-year deal
item.description: The veteran cornerback is enjoying a career renaissance in Atlanta.
item.content:encoded:
Ian Cunningham is not sitting around and waiting to lock up players the Atlanta Falcons feel good about. In fact, he just got his second new contract of the day done with a Falcons defender.

After the team reportedly locked up Cameron Thomas, they’ve signed veteran cornerback C.J. Henderson to a two-year deal. It’s well-deserved for a player who has gone from a first round bust in Jacksonville to a valuable starter in Atlanta, and it means Henderson will likely be in the starting mix at corner for 2027 and beyond. He’s earned it by battling his way up the depth chart here and beginning to really deliver on the promise that once made him a top pick.

Henderson was originally drafted ninth overall in 2020, ahead of fellow Falcons starter A.J. Terrell, and had an up-and-down tenure in Jacksonville that ended when the team shipped him off to Carolina alongside a fifth round pick for a third rounder and a backup tight end. Henderson was a part-time starter with more ups and downs from 2021 to 2023 with Carolina, and spent time with the Texans and Steelers before winding up on Atlanta’s practice squad. He did fine work in limited spot duty in 2025, but was pressed into more significant action with injuries piling up in 2026 and has been solid-to-stellar in every game except the rough matchup against the Bengals last week.

For the year, Henderson has allowed just 54.5% of the passes thrown his way to be completed for 252 yards, 10.5 yards per reception, three touchdowns, and five pass breakups. That completion percentage is the lowest number allowed by any Falcons defensive back this year, and he’s kept his missed tackle rate low while only being penalized once. It’s a renaissance year for Henderson, who has the coaching staff’s trust and is at worst a very high-end backup for Atlanta that they can count on to start for extended stretches when called upon; I would not be surprised if he keeps his starting job all year.

We don’t have the terms of the deal yet, but keeping Henderson around gives the Falcons a quality, deep cornerback corps well into 2028 with A.J. Terrell, Avieon Terrell, Billy Bowman Jr., Sydney Brown, and maybe Mike Hughes all here too. Congratulations to Henderson, and let’s hope he can keep this good thing going.

item.title: Titans’ 3 most important players vs. Jaguars are totally obvious
item.description: Identifying the Tennessee Titans’ three most important players in Sunday’s Week 10 game versus the Jacksonville Jaguars.
item.content:encoded:
Following the NFL trade deadline frenzy, the Tennessee Titans actually play a football game on Sunday. They’ll face the AFC South-leading Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 10. These two franchises are in different spots. While the Titans traded Jeffery Simmons and Amani Hooker away, the Jaguars brought in Jordan Davis, Davon Godchaux, and Jessie Bates III.

The Titans didn’t trade any offensive players during the deadline. They’ll attempt to build on the 36-point success they found versus the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 8. With that in mind, we’ve identified three Titans players who need big-time performances against the Jaguars.

QB Cam Ward

Cam Ward played the best game of his career versus the Bengals in Week 8. It was his first-ever 300 yard passing performance. Ward threw two touchdowns, zero interceptions, and even rushed for a career-high 41 yards. He was accurate, aggressive, decisive, and efficient. The former Miami Hurricanes standout will now look to build on that momentum against a very good Jaguars defense that is being coached by a future HC in Anthony Campanile.

WR Carnell Tate

Titans rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate did not practice earlier this week, but appears to be trending in the correct direction. The fourth overall pick missed the Week 8 Bengals game, but also had the bye week to rest and recover. Tate, who won Offensive Rookie of the Month for October, has shown terrific chemistry with Ward. Despite the Bengals result, the Titans desperately need their playmaking WR1 versus this vaunted Jaguars defense.

RB Tony Pollard

The Titans decided against trading Tony Pollard at the deadline. Their lead running back has rushed for 100+ yards in consecutive appearances, adding five touchdowns across those performances. Pollard’s breakout has coincided with Ward’s breakout, which is partially why the Titans held onto him past the trade deadline. He needs to keep momentum going.

item.title: Falcons announce two-year contract extension with C.J. Henderson
item.description: Falcons cornerback C.J.
item.content:encoded:
Falcons cornerback C.J. Henderson has agreed to a new contract.

The Falcons announced today that Henderson has signed a two-year extension.

This is Henderson's second season on the Falcons, but last year he was mostly a practice squad player who was only active for four games. This year, Henderson has started the last six games at boundary corner after A.J. Terrell went on injured reserve, and Henderson has played very well in his place. Falcons defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich praised Henderson for how well he has played after being thrust into a new role.

"It's been a fun journey with C.J. because when he got here, obviously, he had a very well-known past in this league," Ulbrich said, via the Falcons' website. "To help him start to reinvent himself here, it brings me a ton of joy because he's just such an amazing young man. I'm excited for every opportunity he gets and every opportunity to show this league exactly who he is now, today."

The 28-year-old Henderson entered the NFL with the Jaguars as the ninth overall pick in the 2020 draft. He was a disappointment in Jacksonville and got traded to the Panthers during his second season, and for most of his NFL career he has been viewed as a draft bust. But he got a big opportunity in Atlanta when Terrell went down, and he's made the most of it. Now he's getting rewarded.

item.title: Examining biggest Jets tendencies before Week 10’s game vs. Bills
item.description: Here’s what the Jets like to do on both sides of the ball
item.content:encoded:
The Jets are 2-7 entering Week 10’s game in MetLife Stadium against the Buffalo Bills after Aaron Glenn’s club lost 35-12 against the Chiefs a week ago.

But Gang Green is slightly better than their record indicates.

Let’s dive into New York’s tendencies before this AFC East clash on Sunday.

Jets offense

Geno Smith, pocket passer

On Sunday, the Bills will face their fourth pure pocket passer of the 2026 campaign in Smith. The others being Jared Goff, Matthew Stafford, and Kirk Cousins.

Smith resides that lower-left quadrant, escaping the pocket on on a little over 10% of his dropbacks.

First-round talents

The Jets offense features five former first-round picks at marquee positions. Both of their tackles (Olu Fashanu and Armand Membo) were first-round picks. Two of their receivers (Garrett Wilson and Omar Cooper Jr.) — former selections in the first-round.

And the wild-card of them all, tight end Kenyon Sadiq — first-rounder in 2026.

While some of this talent hasn’t fully acclimated to the NFL just yet, there’s plenty of inherent talent within the Jets offensive unit.

As for Wilson, who missed last week’s contest against the Chiefs, he has the seventh-best Average Separation Score, per Fantasy Points Data, among receivers who’ve run at least 99 routes entering Week 10. And it’s Cooper Jr., not Wilson, who finds himself inside the Top 10 among all qualifying receivers in yards per route run currently at a hefty 2.73.

Minimal motion + play-action

The Jets don’t use a lot of window dressing in their offense. They’re currently owners of the sixth-lowest motion rate at 56.0%. And Smith has used play-action on 25.1% of his dropbacks, the 20th-highest among qualifying quarterbacks.

More than most teams, what you see is what you get with the Jets offensively.

Jets defense

Blitzing + base defense + man coverage

The Bills will get a reprieve from the blitzing extravaganza they experienced in Week 9’s game against the Vikings, but they better stay prepare to deal with extra rushers.

Entering this game, the Jets are fourth in the NFL in blitz rate at 41.2%, per Fantasy Points Data. In most years, that’s probably Top 2 or even the highest in the league. The blitz-happy way is foundational to Glenn’s defenses.

Two other core elements of who the Jets are defensively — they don’t move out of base often (so more linebackers, fewer defensive backs on the field), and they want to man-up in coverage.

New York has the 10th-highest base defense rate 33.3% — two spots lower than the Bills — and play man at the league’s fourth-highest rate (31.7%).

David Bailey

The No. 2 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft has gotten out to an rather productive start to his NFL career.

My No. 1 overall player in the class, whom I gave a “Jared Verse Lite” comparison to, Bailey has 31 pressures through nine games, the 13th-most among all edge rushers in the NFL.

He hasn’t regularly destroyed all left and right tackles in his path as much as the pressure total would indicate, but in Week 9 against the Chiefs, Bailey was genuinely tremendous. He displayed his whole pass-rush arsenal, highlighted by his patented outside speed rush and a speed-to-power based bull.

He’s a big-time talent starting to come into his own getting after the quarterback — 20 of his 31 pressures have occurred in the past four games.

Pass defense vs. run defense

The Jets don’t have the horses up front along the defensive line of a few years ago. But they’re still a stingy run defense thanks to the likes of explosive linebacker Jamien Sherwood and thumping safety Dane Belton.

Discounting garbage time, New York’s defense is currently ninth in the NFL in EPA per rush allowed.

The Jets also no longer boast Sauce Gardner out wide, D.J. Reed in the slot, and Jordan Whitehead at safety. And those truths have taken a toll on their pass defense.

The Jets are 30th in EPA per dropback surrendered and have allowed the fifth-highest passer rating at 103.5.

This matchup calls for the Bills to take to the air.

item.title: 3 keys to a Cincinnati Bengals victory vs. Pittsburgh Steelers
item.description: The Bengals cannot let Jaylen Warren go off for 170 all-purpose yards again this week.
item.content:encoded:
The 6-2 Cincinnati Bengals will host the 6-2 Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday Night Football this week.

The Steelers defeated the Bengals 30-27 earlier this season in Pittsburgh. Can Cincinnati return the favor and take the lead in the AFC North standings?

If they are going to do so, here are three keys to victory.

Contain Jaylen Warren

Jaylen Warren has been playing really well for the Steelers this season. He was a huge reason they were able to get the victory earlier this season against the Bengals. He had almost 170 all-purpose yards during that game. He does damage where the Bengals often struggle against the run, and that is to the outside. He is also an effective pass catcher who can make huge chunk plays out of the backfield.

It will be a group effort to limit Jaylen Warren this week. That starts with the guys up front setting a good edge and forcing Warren to go back inside. Once that happens, they will need the linebackers and secondary players to make the tackle. Warren is elusive, shows good leg drive, and is critical for the success of the Pittsburgh offense. Slowing him down will be one of the biggest keys to earning a tough divisional victory on Sunday night.

Effective running from Chase Brown

Chase Brown ran for over six yards per carry on Sunday against the Falcons. While he has yet to top 100 yards rushing in a game this season, he is starting to be much more effective when his number is called. Last season, when the Bengals faced off against the Steelers at home, Chase Brown had just 11 carries. Even though he had just 11 carries, he was still able to top 100 yards rushing. You don’t have to change your identity, but running effectively will be a big key on Sunday night.

Earlier this season against Pittsburgh, Brown ran for 61 yards on 13 carries. One thing that would certainly help the numbers in the running game would be to play with a lead. Getting an early lead and being able to effectively run the football will go a long way toward trying to get the victory and taking the lead in the division at 7-2.

Protect the football

When the Bengals played the Pittsburgh Steelers earlier this season, they had two crucial turnovers that cost them the game. The first turnover was a muffed punt by Ke’Shawn Williams. Not only did Williams muff the punt, but PJ Jules tried to pick the football up instead of just jumping on it.

That muffed punt came with the Bengals leading 27-24 early in the fourth quarter. The Steelers recovered the fumble and went on to add a field goal. That tied the game at the time at 27-27. After another Pittsburgh field goal put them up 30-27, the Cincinnati Bengals offense came back on the field with a chance to win the game.

The Bengals got the ball with 2:08 left on the clock. After 17-yard and 13-yard completions to Ja’Marr Chase, the Bengals were driving with an opportunity to win the game, or at least send it to overtime. They had the ball at midfield with a first down. This time, Dalton Risner got beat by Derrick Harmon, and Joe Burrow fumbled the ball while looking to get the ball out instead of taking the sack. The Steelers recovered the fumble and won the game 30-27.

If the Bengals can win the turnover battle, they should put themselves in a good position to win the football game. With a win, they will be sitting at the top of the division at 7-2. This is a massive matchup on Sunday Night Football in Cincinnati. There should be an electric atmosphere at Paycor Stadium this week.

item.title: Return to Germany an ‘unbelievable’ experience for Patriots practice squad tackle
item.description: Patriots reserve offensive tackle Lorenz Metz grew up an hour from Munich.
item.content:encoded:
Listed at 6-foot-9, 320 pounds, Lorenz Metz is the tallest player currently under contract with the New England Patriots. Despite his towering height, however, he is largely flying under the radar.

Not only is Metz is a member of the team’s practice squad, but due to his international designation ineligible to play in any games this year. That will not change this week, despite the Patriots set to play the Detroit Lions just 50 miles from his hometown in the German province of Bavaria.

And yet, making the trip back home and getting to practice at the facilities of FC Bayern Munich is a special experience for the 29-year-old.

“I grew up about an hour from here,” he said during a press conference on Thursday. “Bayern Munich was the team. Thomas Müller, [Manuel] Neuer — all of the Bayern players were my role models. And now standing out there on the field is unbelievable.”

Born in Neuötting, a city of 9,000 people east of Munich, Metz’s football journey started as a fan and somebody who couldn’t escape the Patriots even back then.

“I think in 2012 they started showing regular season games in German free TV,” he explained. “2012, 2014, 2016, the Patriots were pretty much on top with Tom Brady. That was the team everybody knew, with Tom Brady, who also everybody knew.”

At the age of 18, Metz started his playing career with the Kirchdorf Wildcats, appearing in 12 games and registering 48 tackles and a sack in his lone season as a defensive lineman. Shortly thereafter, he moved to the United States to play college football at Cincinnati. He switched from defensive to offensive tackle upon arrival, and over the next five seasons saw action in 39 games with 26 starts.

Despite his success and being a one-time first-team All-AAC selection, Metz went unselected in the 2023 NFL Draft. He was initially picked up by the Bears as a free agent and also spent some time in Tampa before joining New England’s practice squad for the playoff run in January.

Nine months later, he gets to experience the Patriots’ trip to Germany — and embracing his role as a local. Not only did he get more than 30 tickets for friends and family for Sunday’s game, he also treated his fellow offensive linemen and a handful of other teammates to dinner on Thursday night.

And despite his status for the game, he is looking forward to it as well. That is especially true with his brother having visited the first ever NFL game in Munich back in 2022.

“I was following it all,” he said about that particular contest between the Seahawks and Buccaneers. “I already was in college in Cinicinnati, couldn’t come to the game unfortunately, but did get two tickets for my brother. So, this is almost like a full-circle moment playing in that game and taking the field.”

item.title: Saints and Panthers Prediction: Showdown for the NFC South
item.description: The Saints look to take the division lead against Panthers
item.content:encoded:
The New Orleans Saints return to action on Sunday as they prepare to host the Carolina Panthers in a crucial NFC South showdown. With both teams looking to strengthen their position in the division standings, Sunday’s matchup presents an important opportunity for the Black and Gold to build momentum as the season enters its second half.

Every game carries added significance for the Saints as they look to overcome their early season struggles and remain in contention for the NFC South title. A victory over a division rival would not only provide a much-needed boost of confidence but also help New Orleans gain valuable ground in the standings as the playoff race begins to take shape.

Saints QB Tyler Shough continues to show flashes of his potential as the future of the franchise. Establishing consistency on offense, protecting the football and capitalizing on scoring opportunities, combined with the emergence of the Saints’ running game, could provide a much-needed spark and help establish a more balanced offensive attack.

On the opposite sideline, Carolina presents a familiar divisional challenge, with quarterback Bryce Young looking to lead the Panthers to a statement victory. Brandon Staley’s defense will need to apply pressure, limit explosive plays and create turnovers to give the Saints an opportunity to come away with the win.

With the lead in the division on the line, can Shough bring the Black and Gold to a much-needed victory, or will Young and the Panthers spoil New Orleans’ hopes of climbing on top of the NFC South?

PREDICTION: Saints 31 – Panthers 27

The Saints capitalize on their home-field advantage in a hard-fought divisional showdown, with Shough delivering a strong performance to lead New Orleans to their second straight victory and the top spot in the division.

item.description: Kansas City has risen to the occasion of stuffing top running backs in 2026.

The bulk of credit for the Kansas City Chiefs’ 6-2 record goes to running back Kenneth Walker. His 872 rushing yards ranks second in the league as Kansas City’s offense has retooled around the prized free agent signing.

For Kansas City to get a seventh win on Sunday in a road game against the Atlanta Falcons, the Chiefs will need a plan to slow down the running back who currently exceeds Walker’s total by eight yards.

On Thursday, the architect of Kansas City’s defense and the unit’s longest-tenured player made it very clear that star running back Bijan Robinson is on their mind.

“We’re trying to play fundamentally sound,” said defensive tackle Chris Jones. “Reset the line of scrimmage with the D-line. He’s a very patient runner — inside and outside. He can break a big one every time his hands are on the ball. For us, it’s about playing fundamental football and playing disciplined.”

Defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo has also noted Robinson’s ability to run both inside and outside — and how quickly he switches between the two.

“Especially [against] this kind of offensive scheme,” the coach explained, “It’s all about first building a wall — it’s interior to get it to go that way. Setting an edge, and I think the most important thing about this guy is tracking the hip. He’s as good as anybody. It might be a designed outside run play, but he ends up and now it feels an inside run play. When you start chasing the outside and get turned, that’s when he goes down hill. That’s why we’re preaching big this week about tracking the hips, so when he does decide to cut it back, we can eliminate some of those explosive runs. I think that’s when he really is effective.”

In their seven games, the Chiefs have allowed a single 100-yard rusher. They have held some of the league’s best backs — including Jonathan Taylor of the Indianapolis Colts and Breece Hall of the New York Jets — under the mark.

Jones believes the guidance from the team’s veteran coaching staff will serve them well again when they face Robinson.

“We’ve got really great coaches and great assistant coaches,” Jones remarked. “Spags calls the defense and puts us in the right position to execute. We do a lot of film study and a lot of watching of the tendencies of a team and what they do best. We try to counterreact to that.”
